_all_articles.title: 特朗普签署行政令把 AI 改叫 SI，推出美国政府对话式问答网站
_all_articles.title_original: 特朗普签署行政令把 AI 改叫 SI，推出美国政府对话式问答网站
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息，美东时间周二（9 月 29 日），美国总统特朗普正式签署行政令，下令所有行政部门和机构 使用“超级智能”（Super Intelligence，简称 SI）一词代替人工智能（AI） 。 特朗普在行政令中表示：美国创新者开创的非凡技术远超“人工智能”一词初次出现时的设想。当今前沿系统的能力远不止模仿或自动化人类智能的离散方面。它们不断放大人类的创造力，解锁新的创造力形式，使美国人能够实现此前在科学、医学及几乎所有其他人类领域中不可能实现的目标。随着这些能力的不断提升， 它们越来越代表着不仅仅是人工智能，更是超级智能的新纪元 。 行政令还称，美国联邦政府使用的术语应反映这些技术的变革能力及其为美国人民创造的无限机遇。因此，“超级智能”一词更恰当地反映了这些技术的潜力、潜力和快速发展的能力。因此，特朗普政府的政策是，在法律允许的最大范围内，行政部门应使用“超级智能”和“SI”来替代“人工智能”和“AI”， 并且不会承认“人工智能”和“AI”在任何适用环境中的使用 。 IT之家注意到，特朗普当天还宣布推出了 America.gov ，这是一个为美国人在线访问联邦政府信息或服务的数字入口，他签署了一项行政令，确保美国联邦机构能够与 America.gov 整合。 现在， 美国人可以在 America.gov 上提出任何问题，并获得最新的答案 。今年晚些时候，美国人将能够在 America.gov 上完成护照续签和医疗保险注册等任务，而不必再被送回“一堆迷宫般的网站”。随着机构整合，更多服务将逐步部署到 America.gov 。

_all_articles.title: OpenAI ChatGPT 插件扩展升级：改进排序与推荐方式，支持 MCP 事件自动化
_all_articles.title_original: OpenAI ChatGPT 插件扩展升级：改进排序与推荐方式，支持 MCP 事件自动化
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息，在北京时间 9 月 30 日凌晨 1 点举行的 OpenAI DevDay 2026 活动中，OpenAI 宣布升级插件扩展。 借助插件扩展，开发者可以直接在 ChatGPT 中构建丰富的应用内体验。现在， 用户可以为插件在侧边栏中设置专属入口 ，构建可供用户一边对话一边工作的交互面板，或为产品支持的文件类型创建查看器。 此外，插件创建工具可以帮助开发者构建插件，重新设计的提交流程则提供更清晰的反馈。 OpenAI 还在改进插件目录和对话中的插件排序与推荐方式 ，帮助用户找到相关插件。用户始终可以自主选择使用哪些插件，并逐一批准其访问权限。 现在， 用户可以将受支持的 ChatGPT 插件接入自己构建的站点 ，让工作空间中的团队成员凭各自的权限登录同一应用，并使用各自连接的数据。OpenAI 还简化了自动化流程的添加和管理，让站点中的共享信息保持最新。（适用于 Business、Enterprise、医疗保健版和 Education 套餐） IT之家从发布会获悉，OpenAI 正在加入对拟议的 MCP 事件规范的支持， 让插件能够在已连接的应用中发生事件时启动自动化流程 。例如，用户可以让 ChatGPT 关注项目看板上的新任务。有新任务时，即使用户不在，ChatGPT 也能阅读关联文档并起草计划。

_all_articles.title: 古尔曼：苹果新任 CEO 特努斯着手全面改革，加快产品开发、精简管理层
_all_articles.title_original: 古尔曼：苹果新任 CEO 特努斯着手全面改革，加快产品开发、精简管理层
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 9 月 29 日消息，彭博社马克 · 古尔曼刚刚报道称，苹果新任 CEO 约翰 · 特努斯（John Ternus）上任不到一个月，便已着手对公司内部展开大刀阔斧的改革。 特努斯希望调整公司组织和产品开发方式， 目标包括加快产品研发节奏、扩大硬件产品线，并精简管理层，将更多资源和决策重心放在工程团队上 。当然，相关方案目前仍处于内部讨论阶段。 特努斯于 9 月 1 日正式接替蒂姆 · 库克（Tim Cook）出任 CEO，库克则转任董事会执行主席。特努斯此前担任苹果硬件工程高级副总裁，长期负责 Mac、iPhone、AirPods 等产品的硬件开发。 据知情人士透露，特努斯希望减少对传统春秋两次发布会的依赖，让苹果全年更加频繁地推出新品。同时， 他还希望削减部分中层管理职位，打破工程师与公司高层之间的间隔 。 特努斯曾在负责硬件工程期间向员工表达过类似观点， 希望苹果减少人员扩张、让现有工程师承担更多工作，并降低组织结构中的冗余 。如今，这种思路开始进一步影响苹果内部的组织调整。 过去两周内，苹果硬件工程部门已经开始裁撤部分工程项目经理（EPM）职位。EPM 长期负责产品开发时间表以及跨团队协调，其中部分被裁职位涉及约 6 名董事级管理人员。 这部分员工可在数周时间寻找内部转岗的机会，未能成功转岗的员工将在今年晚些时候离职 。 与此同时，苹果近期还在多个部门进行了规模较小的裁员，并提前削减或取消部分处于早期开发阶段、被认为对公司营收贡献有限的项目， 涉及 Siri、Vision Pro 以及 AI 软件工程等团队 ，部分裁员与员工绩效挂钩。另外，苹果 Fitness+ 团队近期也进行了少量人员调整，该团队此前正在开发仅包含音频内容的健身课程。 人工智能也被特努斯视为提高研发效率的重要工具。苹果今年夏季曾制定一项计划，考虑裁减约 5000 名 AppleCare 客服人员，其中包括大量远程办公员工，原因是公司认为改进后的 AI 电话及网页客服已经足以承担部分相关工作。不过，苹果最终暂缓了这一计划，目前并未推进该批裁员。 尽管如此，部分苹果员工预计今年晚些时候或 2027 年初仍可能出现进一步人员调整。面向 2027 年的早期规划会议中，一些部门曾讨论增加预算和员工数量，但部分预算增幅随后被削减，部分团队则被要求维持与上一年度相同的人员规模，同时压缩营销支出。 苹果还面临关键零部件成本上升的压力。古尔曼指出，当前存储芯片价格高涨推高了苹果的采购成本，公司已经通过提高部分产品售价来抵消成本上涨的影响， 同时也自行消化了一部分增加的成本 。 在产品开发方面，特努斯要求相关管理人员加快推进速度。知情人士表示，目前产品开发团队面临更高的交付要求，需要在更短周期内推出更多产品。苹果原有的研发体系和发布节奏已经运行多年，因此若全面改变，可能需要数年时间。 与此同时，特努斯还与苹果服务业务负责人埃迪 · 库伊（Eddy Cue）、首席财务官凯万 · 帕雷克（Kevan Parekh）讨论新的增收来源，包括推出新的服务，以及提高现有产品和服务的收入贡献。 服务业务长期以来是苹果增长速度较快、利润率较高的业务之一，可以在硬件销售出现波动时提供补充。不过，苹果服务业务的增长动力近期有所减弱。公司 2026 财年第三季度营收达到 1,094 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 7,353.41 亿元人民币） ，同比增长 16%，其中服务业务仍创下同期营收纪录。 特努斯上任后的产品规划也相当密集。苹果预计将在 2027 年推出包括配备摄像头的 AirPods、首款智能眼镜以及为纪念 iPhone 诞生 20 周年而重新设计的 iPhone 等多款新产品。 如果苹果进一步提高产品发布频率，公司将获得更多销售硬件、推动用户使用新服务以及提高现有生态系统收入的机会。不过，目前相关组织改革和产品节奏调整仍处于推进阶段，苹果尚未公开确认具体方案。

_all_articles.title: 创企 TakeMe2Space 将用 SpaceX 火箭送星上天，号称印度首颗轨道计算卫星
_all_articles.title_original: 创企 TakeMe2Space 将用 SpaceX 火箭送星上天，号称印度首颗轨道计算卫星
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 9 月 28 日消息，据路透社今天（28 日）上午报道，印度太空初创公司 TakeMe2Space 计划于当地时间 10 月 1 日搭乘 SpaceX 火箭发射 MOI-1A，并称其为印度首颗轨道计算卫星。与把原始数据全部传回地球不同，TakeMe2Space 希望直接 在轨完成数据处理 。 ▲ 图源 TakeMe2Space，仅供参考 MOI-1A 重量不到 50kg，搭载英伟达 Orin NX 边缘计算处理器，随 SpaceX 的 Transporter-18 拼车任务发射。 TakeMe2Space 披露，MOI-1A 任务已获得地理信息系统公司、教育机构等 23 家客户。创始人兼 CEO 罗纳克 · 萨曼特雷表示，商业客户覆盖农业、采矿、供应链管理和保险等行业，美国太空数据分析公司 Little Place Labs 也在客户名单之中。 客户可以把容器化 AI 模型上传至 MOI-1A。卫星经过指定区域上空时，可直接处理采集的数据， 只把分析结果传回地球，无需下传完整的底层数据集 。“真正能从我们第一代卫星中看到价值的，是那些原本需要花钱下载大量原始数据，再自行进行计算的客户。省下数据下载成本后，就能抵消他们为在轨计算支付的额外费用。” MOI-1A 本质上是一颗具备星载算力的卫星（IT之家注：并非传统数据中心），功率约为 150W。SpaceX 和 Starcloud 等公司则计划采用更先进的英伟达芯片。 TakeMe2Space 的长期目标是建造 尺寸更大、彼此联网的卫星 ，并让单颗卫星能够同时服务多家客户。 TakeMe2Space 在 2024 年底执行过一次技术验证任务，成功验证了上传应用程序、在轨运行 AI 推理并下载结果的能力。随后发射的 MOI-1 则因运载火箭第三级故障而损失。 TakeMe2Space 还计划为关键数据提供在轨冷存储服务，面向希望在地面云服务商之外增加一处备份地点的金融服务和国防领域客户。 该公司透露，大部分卫星子系统均在印度自行设计和制造，芯片、太阳能电池和推进系统则向外部供应商采购。公司计划从 2027 年起推出更大型卫星，提高计算能力并降低成本。

_all_articles.title: 国际货币基金组织：今年全球 AI 投资规模或突破 2 万亿美元
_all_articles.title_original: 国际货币基金组织：今年全球 AI 投资规模或突破 2 万亿美元
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 9 月 25 日消息，国际货币基金组织（IMF）最新年报指出，人工智能有望成为推动全球生产率和投资增长的重要力量，但也可能加剧劳动力市场压力并带来金融风险。 据估算，2025 年与 AI 有关的技术投资为美国 GDP 增速贡献了 0.5 个百分点。美国生产率增速过去几年也有所加快，部分增幅或与 AI 应用初期产生的影响有关。 根据部分外部估算，2026 年全球由私营部门推动的 AI 投资规模 或将突破 2 万亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 13.43 万亿元人民币） ，成为近年来增长最快的经济增长动力之一。 随着全球支出逐步转向 在各行业部署 AI ，AI 带来的生产率提升有望在更多行业和职业中加快。亚洲正积极争取 AI 带来的发展机遇。新加坡凭借完善的数字基础设施、教育体系和前瞻性监管，在 IMFAI 准备度指数中排名第一。 东亚是全球芯片制造和设计中心，东南亚则依托自身制造业优势，进一步向价值链高端迈进 。 风险同样存在。政策制定者、家庭和企业越来越关注 AI 将给劳动力市场带来何种变化，这其中包括替代更多岗位，并压低部分劳动者的工资。 IMF 研究发现， 需要 AI 技能的岗位薪酬更高 ，但这类岗位较多的城市和地区 并没有出现整体就业增长 。 具备 AI 技能的劳动者正在受益，为高收入者提供服务的低技能劳动者也能受益。相比之下， 岗位高度容易受到自动化冲击的中等技能劳动者 并未分享到这些收益。

_all_articles.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
_all_articles.title_original: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiation treatment planning requires balancing competing objectives to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physicians' preferences. This study aims to develop an evidence-driven, multi-agent compound AI system that integrates DRL-based automated treatment planning with LLM-based conversational plan refinement for proton PBS therapy. A policy network trained using PPO first generates multiple plans without human intervention, from which one is selected as the target plan and the others serve as references for subsequent refinements. For challenging cases requiring further adjustments, an LLM-based multi-agent system enables plan refinement through natural language interactions. The system comprises a planning agent that recommends evidence-supported adjustments, a chatbot providing a unified conversational interface, and an evaluation agent that retrieves clinical metrics and identifies constraint violations. To enhance domain-specific reasoning, the planning agent based on Qwen3-14B is designed to justify its recommendations using evidence from previously generated plans and post-trained on task-specific data using SFT and GRPO. The framework was trained and evaluated using 21 patients with H&N cancers, with 5 PPO-generated plans per patient. Of these, 50 plans were selected for instruction-guided refinement. Compared with the base LLM, the post-trained Qwen3-14B demonstrated improved instruction-following, information retrieval and domain-specific reasoning capabilities. The resulting adjustments more effectively improved user-prioritized objectives while limiting deterioration in competing objectives, yielding more clinically appropriate trade-offs in patient-specific plan refinement. The proposed compound AI system provides a user-friendly planning platform, offering a promising approach to personalized proton PBS treatment planning.

_all_articles.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
_all_articles.title_original: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. Across six three-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU. It also supports zero-shot super-resolution and efficient closed-form spatial derivatives. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29.2-million-node MAST-U tokamak model.

_all_articles.title: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk
_all_articles.title_original: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk
_all_articles.summary: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk Mistral are back in the game. Today they're releasing a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1 trillion parameter, 49 billion active parameter model trained on their own cluster of 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The preview is available via their API. They promise to release the open weights model at the "end of this month". The model only supports two reasoning levels - "none" and "high" - via the Mistral API. Here are both pelicans - the "high" one looks better, though surprisingly it only used 2,717 output tokens compared to "none" which used 3,275: On Artificial Analysis it scores 38 , just behind DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, which is a 552B model. It's a huge improvement on last December's Mistral Large 3, which drew this terrible pelican and scored 9 on AA . It's certainly not a Fable-class model, but it's great to see Mistral put out a model that's back to being maybe about 6 months behind the frontier. Via Hacker News Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , mistral , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , llm-release

_all_articles.title: Text2Dashboard: A Governed Agent Architecture for Natural-Language Dashboard Generation over Enterprise DataBrain
_all_articles.title_original: Text2Dashboard: A Governed Agent Architecture for Natural-Language Dashboard Generation over Enterprise DataBrain
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.06914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text2Dashboard is a DataBrain-specific prototype that turns natural-language analytic requests into inspectable dashboards. An installable Codex plugin and standalone Agent Runtime combine schema-constrained model decisions with typed tools, persistent state, and deterministic Hooks for approval, audit, checkpointing, recovery, and failure handling. The pipeline resolves entities, discovers metadata, enforces read-only SQL, composes dashboards, and applies static checks, dynamic preflight, and browser inspection. The model proposes actions while deterministic software controls execution and records state transitions. We evaluate the workflow on frozen real-DataBrain tasks and controlled Hook faults. Strict success was 6/8 on metadata and SQL tasks: metadata selection passed 4/4, all four SQL tasks met semantic criteria, and 2/4 met the exact output-column contract. The final release passed 4/4 single-panel dashboard tasks, one two-panel task, and one existing-dashboard refinement; a parameterised task exceeded its step limit. All ten fault scenarios met their specified outcomes without unapproved external side effects. Model inference accounted for over 97\% of observed runtime in every reported group. These small, DataBrain-specific results do not establish production readiness, general text-to-SQL accuracy, or an efficiency advantage over manual dashboard construction.

_all_articles.title: Measuring the Microtask Eligibility Gap: When Is an Off-the-Shelf SLM Enough for an Agent Harness?
_all_articles.title_original: Measuring the Microtask Eligibility Gap: When Is an Off-the-Shelf SLM Enough for an Agent Harness?
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.00025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses increasingly want to run small language models (SLMs) on the microtasks around a frontier large language model (LLM) planner: auto-approving shell commands, writing memory, selecting tools, ranking past turns. We ask whether off-the-shelf SLMs meet practitioner-defined thresholds and, when they fail, why, and whether quantization changes the answer. We build a benchmark of 4 such microtasks with fixed prompts and automatic metrics, each with a pre-specified threshold $\tau$ anchored to a cheap non-LLM baseline and a CI-aware eligibility rule (a configuration passes only if its confidence bound clears $\tau$). Sweeping Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B at their best (FP16, greedy, one frozen prompt, no tuning), we find an eligibility gap: 0 of 16 (4 tasks $\times$ 4 models) configurations pass (verified by checking the raw outputs and parser behavior). A logprob decision-threshold diagnostic (T1/T3/T4; T2 via a context-length/cascade probe) separates the failures into capability deficits and failures that can be addressed by changing the decoding threshold (4 regimes). Quantization to 4-bit (RTN/GPTQ/AWQ) does damage that depends on model size and moves no configuration into eligibility (certified on the reconstructable hard-label tasks T1/T3, diagnostic/windowed robustness on T2/T4), so the gap tracks model size more than precision; it replicates on Llama-3.x (12/12 ineligible) and is robust to the anchor choice (a $\tau$-sweep) and to prompt wording (0/112 eligible across the original plus 3 neutral paraphrases per cell). The practical implication: place SLMs behind a baseline that meets the CI-backed threshold, and use the SLM only where the baseline fails to meet the threshold; e.g. a 4B re-ranker over a BM25 shortlist beats BM25 ($+0.047$ [0.020, 0.073], without itself certifying eligibility).

_all_articles.title: ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision
_all_articles.title_original: ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.35954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model post-training generates self-generated rollouts through reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation, yet this experience is often treated as stale once the policy advances. Historical rollouts can remain compatible with a later policy while preserving behaviors that the policy no longer expresses reliably. However, they may also contain mistakes, abandoned attempts, and redundant actions that should not be imitated, motivating finer-grained selective supervision. We introduce ROSS (Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision), which preserves the full historical trajectory as context while applying loss only to selected model-generated continuations. Across domain-specific reinforcement learning, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and agentic reinforcement learning, ROSS consistently improves upstream checkpoints and outperforms baselines across mathematics, code generation, instruction following, and software engineering. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, ROSS improves the six-benchmark MOPD average from 58.40% to 62.20% and SWE-bench Verified from 64.20% to 68.40%. These results show that self-rollout training leaves behind reusable behavioral experience that can yield further gains through offline supervised fine-tuning (SFT), without additional policy rollouts.

_all_articles.title: Self-Evolving Harness on Multiple Tasks with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
_all_articles.title_original: Self-Evolving Harness on Multiple Tasks with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.38372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A harness is the code around a language-model agent that organizes prompts, calls tools, manages context, and controls execution. As models grow stronger, recent work has begun to let agents improve their own harnesses, a line of work known as self-evolving harnesses. In most existing methods, a separate proposer running on a human-designed harness modifies the solver's harness, and a separate harness is evolved for each benchmark. Real-world tasks come from many domains, so both the evolution and the evaluation of a harness should cover a diverse range of tasks. We propose a framework close to recursive self-improvement: the same frozen model, on the same version of the harness, first solves tasks as the solver and then, as the proposer, reads the complete run records and directly edits the harness that runs it. Each evolution batch draws tasks from five benchmarks in different domains. To measure generalization, training and held-out tasks are strictly separated, and we additionally evaluate on five out-of-distribution benchmarks never used during evolution. We frame the evolution process as deep-learning training with two stages, multi-task pretraining and continual training. Starting from a 49-line seed harness, the harness obtained at the end of the first stage improves the average score by 4.48 points on the in-distribution benchmarks and by 12.64 points on the out-of-distribution benchmarks, surpassing Codex on the former and matching it on the latter. In the second stage, continued evolution on Claw-Eval, one of the out-of-distribution benchmarks, further raises the score on that benchmark from 66.17 to 68.06, exceeding Codex. We also provide an in-depth analysis of the mechanisms that emerged during evolution, including output truncation, history compaction, and independent review.

_all_articles.title: Pistis Technical Report
_all_articles.title_original: Pistis Technical Report
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Pistis model family, comprising 27B- and 9B-parameter multimodal large language models built on Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5, respectively, and developed through a general and scalable post-training framework. The framework first establishes a strong foundation through large-scale multimodal supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Building on this SFT foundation, we propose Interleaved Distillation and Reinforcement Learning (IDRL), a novel post-training paradigm that tightly integrates on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning within a single training loop. By alternating between the two objectives, rather than optimizing either in isolation or combining them in a static joint loss, IDRL enables more effective knowledge transfer, greater optimization stability, and more precise credit assignment for long-horizon agentic trajectories, leading to stronger performance while mitigating common capability trade-offs. At both model scales, the framework produces two specialized variants: Pistis-Thinking, designed to strengthen deep multimodal reasoning, and Pistis-Agentic, which additionally incorporates agentic trajectory data to support long-horizon planning, iterative reasoning, and tool use. Pistis-Agentic is particularly strong in multimodal search. Both scales outperform their corresponding base models. Beyond model-parameter optimization, we further introduce Pistis-Auto-Harnessing (PAH), a system-level method that automatically improves the agent's inference harness through iterative optimization. Experiments demonstrate that PAH enhances the model performance without updating the model parameters or increasing the interaction budget.

_all_articles.title: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design
_all_articles.title_original: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.20628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. The post-training method for such generators remains a limitation: a corpus lists the graphs that solved a query but never ranks them, leaving continued supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with no per-query preference to exploit. Without such a preference, the generator drifts toward the topologies the corpus contains most often rather than those that suit each query, so a gain on one task can come at a cost on another. We propose PRISM, which recovers per-query signal from the same corpus by learning with privileged information: a teacher reads, through a zero-initialized low-rank branch, a sibling graph that also solved the query and is unavailable at deployment, and the student matches its per-decision targets on trajectories the student samples itself. Across six diverse benchmarks PRISM improves over every topology-design baseline evaluated, and matched-teacher controls support the contribution of privileged query information. Code is available in this link.

_all_articles.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
_all_articles.title_original: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective cross-model collaboration. Specifically, \textit{model slicing} replaces a large model with smaller, heterogeneous models under a comparable parameter budget, enabling prior reasoning to be reassessed across distinct model parameterizations. \textit{Pyramid supervision} combines protocol distillation with step-level supervision to refine reasoning and interaction decisions throughout collaboration. We evaluate our approach across four task categories: multi-hop question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and open-ended constrained generation. The trained heterogeneous models achieve comparable or better task performance than the original large model and established multi-agent baselines, including reinforcement-learning-based methods, while also achieving higher inference efficiency than the multi-agent baselines and exhibiting differentiated collaboration patterns across tasks. These findings show that learned collaboration turns model heterogeneity into complementary reasoning capabilities.

_all_articles.title: 消息称月之暗面完成上市前最后一轮融资：估值约 500 亿美元，计划明年一季度赴港 IPO
_all_articles.title_original: 消息称月之暗面完成上市前最后一轮融资：估值约 500 亿美元，计划明年一季度赴港 IPO
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据彭博社报道，知情人士消息，月之暗面（Moonshot AI）已经完成上市前最后一轮私募融资，估值约 500 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,357.23 亿元人民币） ；该公司计划于明年第一季度在香港进行首次公开募股（IPO）。 部分知情人士称，这家国内头部人工智能企业已经开始筹备投资者摸底沟通，最早将于本月就开展先期意向会议，以此评估资本市场态度。 月之暗面是中国 AI 赛道当中最受瞩目的企业之一。今年 7 月，Kimi K3 开源大模型正式发布，一举站上全球舞台；在多项评测指标上，该模型几乎可以同 OpenAI、Anthropic 的头部模型相抗衡。其 IPO 也成为港股市场最受期待的交易项目之一。眼下 AI 驱动的新股融资活动正在香港接连刷新纪录。知情人士表示，本次 IPO 计划的募资上限为 50 亿美元。 《The Information》指出，监管机构已经针对深度求索（DeepSeek）与月之暗面启动数据安全调查，国内 AI 行业随之迎来更严格的监管。尚不清楚监管环境的变化会对公司估值以及 IPO 时间进度造成何种影响，市场对于企业治理与安全层面的担忧也有所上升。 知情人士表示，各项工作仍处在磋商阶段，IPO 时间表依然存在变数。 经过多轮融资，这家公司的估值持续走高。今年夏天上一轮融资完成时，估值为 315 亿美元。知情人士透露，公司的年度经常性收入（ARR，用来衡量未来营收规模）当前为 10 亿美元，预计到 12 月将攀升至 20 亿美元。此前彭博社曾报道，在今年 6 月，该公司的 ARR 为 3 亿美元。 此前知情人士就曾透露，这家总部位于北京的 AI 实验室已经委任美国银行担任本次 IPO 的整体协调人；保荐银行则包括中金公司、德意志银行以及高盛集团。该公司已经以保密方式向港交所递交 IPO 申请。 月之暗面于 2023 年初成立，创始人杨植麟原为清华大学教授，此前曾先后任职于 Meta Platforms 以及谷歌（Alphabet）。阿里巴巴、腾讯以及五源资本（5Y Capital）都是该公司的投资方。

_all_articles.title: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
_all_articles.title_original: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EHR foundation models promise scalable clinical prediction across health systems, yet their deployment is constrained by a tokenization bottleneck. The same clinical concept can appear as different ontology codes, local identifiers, synonyms, or free-text descriptions, which standard EHR tokenizers treat as unrelated symbols. A model trained on MIMIC-III with a closed-vocabulary tokenizer can use only 13% of eICU events. We introduce MEDIATOR, a discrete ontology-agnostic tokenizer that maps any clinical concept expressed as text into a shared vector-quantized codebook, turning EHR harmonization into open-vocabulary tokenization without manual mappings or a fixed vocabulary. Trained with synonym supervision and guided by enriched concept descriptions, code co-occurrence, and relation graphs, MEDIATOR collapses equivalent expressions while organizing distinct concepts in a medically meaningful discrete space. Used as the token interface of an EHR Transformer, MEDIATOR improves mean AUPRC over the strongest prior tokenizer by 4.0 points (8% relative) on 20 MIMIC-III tasks and by 8.6 points (29% relative) in zero-shot transfer to 14 eICU tasks, where it uses all events. The transfer gain combines coverage and representation, as MEDIATOR remains the best tokenizer under identical inputs (+1.0 and +1.9 points on operational and subcohort-mortality tasks). Same-encoder controls show that the text encoder drives in-domain accuracy, while the learned objectives of MEDIATOR drive transfer robustness and entity-linking quality. MEDIATOR also enables transferable attribution across hospitals.

_all_articles.title: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels
_all_articles.title_original: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage. Combining public datasets is challenging because their taxonomies differ, and even after categories are mapped to a common schema, labels can disagree on what counts as a detection, producing inconsistent training and evaluation signals. To address these problems, we present a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. Evaluated on the AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII benchmarks at a low-FPR operating point, our model achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons under our labels and 9 of 14 under the original labels. Its largest recall gains include useful additional coverage, such as multilingual disclosures and IP addresses embedded in URLs. It achieves this with 2-10x higher throughput and 94-97% less peak GPU memory than the baselines, delivering leading detection performance at substantially lower cost.

_all_articles.title: NASA 公布月球探测车最新进展：VIPER 计划 2027 年探测月球南极水冰资源
_all_articles.title_original: NASA 公布月球探测车最新进展：VIPER 计划 2027 年探测月球南极水冰资源
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）当地时间 10 月 20 日公布了月球探测车最新研发进展及任务规划。 NASA 表示，用于探测月球水冰等资源的“挥发物调查极地探索车”（VIPER）计划于 2027 年前往月球南极地区，载人月球地形车（LTV）则计划于 2028 年运抵月球南极地区，为未来载人探月任务和月球基地建设提供支持。 据 NASA 官方公告，VIPER 目前已在美国约翰逊航天中心完成组装，正在进行最后阶段的测试，之后将转运至肯尼迪航天中心，为发射做准备。IT之家查询获悉，该探测车计划搭乘蓝色起源的第二艘“蓝月”MK1 月球着陆器前往月球，预计于 2027 年底抵达月球南极地区。 VIPER 的主要任务是在月球南极地区寻找水冰及其他挥发性资源，并绘制相关资源分布图。NASA 计划让探测车进入永久阴影陨坑开展调查，研究不同深度、温度和土壤环境中的资源情况，为评估月球原位资源利用潜力提供数据。NASA 表示，相关探测结果也将帮助研究人员了解月球水资源的来源与分布，并为未来长期月面活动提供参考。 载人月球地形车方面，NASA 表示，已选择 Astrolab 和 Lunar Outpost 参与首阶段月球地形车研发，并计划通过商业合作方式将车辆送往月球南极地区。蓝色起源将承担相关月球运输任务，目标是在 2028 年交付车辆。 NASA 介绍，载人月球地形车属于不加压月面车辆，可搭载宇航员和货物，在宇航员执行舱外活动时提供地面交通支持。在载人任务到达前，这些车辆还可由地球远程操控，用于绘制月面地形图、收集环境数据，并测试车辆在极端温度、光照变化和永久阴影区域中的运行能力。 NASA 表示，机器人探测车与载人月球地形车将共同支持月球基地建设的早期阶段。前者侧重于调查水冰等资源，后者则用于月面运输、科学调查和环境测绘，相关数据将为未来月球表面移动系统及基础设施设计提供依据。

_all_articles.title: 研究发现：AI 可篡改人类记忆，植入从未发生的虚假事件
_all_articles.title_original: 研究发现：AI 可篡改人类记忆，植入从未发生的虚假事件
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，据 Washington Post 报道，研究发现，AI 可篡改人类记忆。这项实验一开始准备了 24 张普通照片：婚礼、城市街道、赛跑场景。麻省理工学院媒体实验室教授帕蒂 · 梅斯（Pattie Maes）和同事把这些照片展示给了 200 名受试者。 短暂休息后，一部分人再次看到原图；另一部分人看到经过 AI 修改的版本 —— 人物面部表情被改动、画面中新增军人形象，或是添加气候变化相关景象。 随后研究人员开展记忆测试。 梅斯看到结果时感到震惊： 观看 AI 篡改图片的受试者，产生错误记忆的概率大幅上升 。更严重的是，她表示，他们对这些虚假记忆的自信程度反而更高。 梅斯说：“基本上，我认为这一切非常危险。” 到目前为止，公众的担忧大多集中在一些研究者所说的“认知放弃”：随着机器承担越来越多思考类工作，人们会越来越不愿、也越来越没有能力去审视机器给出的信息。但还有一种可能性受到的关注要少得多： AI 或许正在改变我们的记忆本身。 一批针对政治事件、罪案甚至新电影认知的新研究表明，AI 生成的图像与对话，可以把虚假细节植入人脑，让人们笃定地相信某些从未发生过的事情真实存在。 记忆不只是留存过去。它提供知识与经验，帮助我们理解当下、预判未来，塑造自我认知、维系人际关系，同时指导个人与集体做出决策。 然而记忆本身也是人类心智一大短板：我们只能记住所经历事物的一小部分，细节会消失，回忆会变得模糊，每次回想时记忆本身还会发生改变。 AI 看上去恰好可以弥补这些缺陷：它能存储海量信息、秒级检索，找回人类可能永久遗失的细节。但这些特性同样带来潜在风险。AI 系统不只是存储过去，它还会解读、总结、重构过往信息，并且有时会出错。 其后果远不止记错一张照片、一段对话那么简单。从车祸到性侵案件，法庭审理常常依赖证人回忆，尽管数十年研究早已证明，目击者记忆极易被扭曲。而历史本身，取决于个人与社会选择保留、遗忘，以及最终愿意相信的往事。 人类记忆天生存在缺陷 梅斯是人工智能领域先驱。在长达 35 年以上的职业生涯早期，她参与开发了部分奠定早期互联网基础的算法。但长期以来，她更感兴趣的是 AI 的另一种可能性：不是机器取代人类智能，而是拓展人类智能。 对梅斯而言，这个问题带有个人情感。随着年岁增长，她母亲开始遗忘日常生活的片段。 “我母亲会忘记昨天谁来过、别人跟她说了什么，”梅斯说，她只能自己写便条：“‘女儿说两周后会过来’。” 梅斯开始构想比记事本强大得多的工具：一款记忆助手，可以默默记录一个人的生活轨迹。 对于阿尔茨海默病及其他痴呆症患者，这个课题尤为紧迫。这类疾病以记忆丧失为典型特征，会剥夺患者独立生活的能力。 梅斯的研究团队已经搭建了数代外部记忆系统。Memoro 和 MemPal 依托 AI，搭配可穿戴或随身携带的设备，采集日常生活片段，方便后续调取。忘记对话里别人说了什么？可以向系统查询。不记得钥匙放在哪？系统或许能定位。 这套思路不是让衰老的大脑努力提升记忆力，而是给它接入另一套记忆库。 针对老年人的早期测试结果前景向好。梅斯说，她现年 96 岁的母亲认知衰退过重，已经无法从这项技术获益。但这位科学家非常乐观，这类系统未来能够帮助大量人群，在自身生物记忆衰退时维持独立生活。市面上已经出现部分同类商用产品：比如录入个人生平的交互式回忆工具、辅助刷牙等日常活动的个性化智能眼镜。 可如果机器成为我们记忆的延伸，我们自身形成的记忆又会怎样？ 越来越依赖 AI 梅斯另一组研究，为这个问题提供了清晰佐证。 去年发布、目前正在接受同行评审的一项实验中，54 名受试者被要求撰写 SAT 风格作文，主题例如幸福的意义。一组人不使用任何网络工具；第二组可以使用谷歌搜索，但不能调用 AI 生成答案；第三组可以使用 ChatGPT。 写作过程中，头皮电极记录大脑电活动，差异十分明显：独立写作的受试者，大脑不同区域之间的神经连接最强、分布最广；使用谷歌的受试者居中；使用 ChatGPT 的受试者大脑连接最弱。 后续让受试者复述自己刚刚写下的作文，依赖 ChatGPT 的人很难回忆起自己写过的文字。 据IT之家了解，记忆并不是简单地把信息存入大脑。注意力、主观努力、信息提取、建立关联，所有这些过程共同巩固记忆。生成式 AI 会省去其中一部分脑力工作。 宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院市场营销副教授吉迪恩 · 纳夫（Gideon Nave）与伦敦国王学院助理教授史蒂文 · 肖（Steven Shaw）研究 AI 对人类认知的影响，他们提出更深层的担忧。纳夫并不太担心好莱坞式的噩梦 —— 超级 AI 夺取人类控制权，而是一种更隐蔽的风险：人类会慢慢不再锻炼那些机器可以代劳的能力。 “更有可能发生的是人类自身能力退化，而非 AI 接管世界，”他补充，担心未来“思考变成一件可选项”。 研究者称之为“技能退化”的迹象已经出现。肖提到多项研究：习惯借助 AI 辅助工作的人（比如依靠 AI 诊断癌症的医生），一旦失去这套辅助工具，工作表现会下滑。 2025 年发表在《柳叶刀 · 胃肠病学和肝病学》上的一项研究就揭示了这类潜在影响。研究人员观察 19 名资深医生对近 1500 例结肠镜检查的评估，发现医生常态化使用 AI 之后，独立检出癌前病变的能力下降约 20%。 “他们不再像从前那样锻炼这项脑力，”他说，“用进废退。” 对于儿童，他担心更根本的问题：他们可能在核心认知能力尚未完全发育时，就把脑力任务外包给 AI。“他们可能从一开始就无法培养关键的批判性思维能力。” 当然，这不代表使用 ChatGPT 等 AI 工具就一定会让人能力下降。现有近期研究并未证明普通 AI 使用必然造成认知衰退或永久性记忆损伤。相关研究尚处于早期阶段，人类长久以来都在借助工具外包记忆与思考：算盘、钟表、词典、计算器都是如此。 但生成式 AI 带来新的变数。我们越来越依赖它解读检索到的信息，而且人们很容易采信 AI 给出的内容。纳夫与肖的实验中，受试者即便收到错误信息，依然会在很高比例上听从 AI 的建议。 AI 出错时会发生什么？ 本周，AI 伦理与社会领域研究者在瑞典马尔默举办年度会议，很多人聚焦同一个问题：当人工智能开始干预人类记忆，后果如何？ 越来越多研究表明，生成式 AI 会以惊人持久的方式干扰记忆：扭曲记忆、模糊自身想法与机器生成内容的边界，甚至植入从未发生事件的记忆。 一项研究中，研究者让受试者观看一段犯罪视频，之后由生成式 AI 聊天机器人对其问询，受试者产生虚假记忆的数量是对照组的三倍。另一项实验，受试者分别在有无 AI 辅助的条件下构思创意；一周之后，他们难以分清哪些想法来自机器、哪些属于自己。 其他实验显示，AI 生成的虚假信息，可以让人记住根本不存在的事情。有一项实验，近半数受试者虚假记得一些从未拍摄的电影翻拍版，其中包括由威尔 · 史密斯主演的《黑客帝国》。另一项实验，AI 生成视频让人们相信自己记得从未发生的政治丑闻。不过研究者指出，深度伪造视频在制造虚假记忆方面，效果并非稳定优于纯文本。 最新研究证据显示，这个问题比研究者预想的更难解决。 企业与政府机构都在争相部署 AI：警方尝试用 AI 总结执法记录仪录像，医院用 AI 整理医疗资料。乔治城大学海量数据研究所助理研究员玛蒂亚 · 西姆（Mattea Sim）表示，最常见的安全保障手段就是保留人工介入，由人排查机器错误。 但这套方案的前提，是人类可以独立核验机器。西姆的研究表明，影响方向可能反过来：AI 会改变人们用来排查 AI 错误的判断与记忆，让人工监督这层保障从根本上失效。 在近期一项实验中，西姆招募 331 人观看一段汽车撞倒行人的简短动画视频。一两天后，受试者阅读一份 AI 生成的事故摘要。一部分人拿到的摘要准确描述视频里的交通标识；另一部分人拿到的摘要由 AI 自信给出错误标识信息。 拿到准确摘要的受试者中，近 84% 能正确记住标识；拿到误导性摘要的受试者，正确率仅约 45%。就算提前告知受试者这份摘要是 AI 生成，也无法避免被它影响。 “大家普遍知道 AI 会犯错，”西姆说，但研究显示，“人工监督或许并不是解决这个问题的好办法。”

_all_articles.title: 研究人员开发 AI 系统：可通过 Wi‑Fi 信号识别隐藏手枪
_all_articles.title_original: 研究人员开发 AI 系统：可通过 Wi‑Fi 信号识别隐藏手枪
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，瑞典国防研究局（FOI）的一组 AI 研究人员开发出一套 AI 系统，能够利用 Wi‑Fi 信号识别隐藏的手枪，可以作为可见光摄像头、笨重金属探测器之外的非侵入式替代方案。相关论文于 10 月 13 日发布在 arXiv 平台，这套名为 WiFireNet 的系统，通过分析物体对环境 Wi‑Fi 信号造成扰动所产生的信道状态信息（CSI）完成识别。整套系统由 Wi‑Fi 发射端、接收端以及 WiFireNet 人工智能模型构成。 普通 Wi‑Fi 信号在传播途中遇到物体时，会根据物体的形状、摆放角度与材质，发生穿透和反射，产生独有的信号特征。这类数据就是信道状态信息，对其分析可以实现较高精度的物体识别。安全领域研究人员此前已经公开过一项技术：普通 Wi‑Fi 路由器识别人体的准确率可达 99.5%。 为搭建 WiFireNet 系统，研究人员首先构建了名为 WiFire Dataset 的数据集。他们同步录制 RGB 视频，同时采集携带各类物品（从手机到手枪）行走的人所反射的 Wi‑Fi 信号。研究人员在这份海量数据集上训练深度学习模型，借助视频片段，把隐藏手枪的视觉特征和它对应的 Wi‑Fi 特征（信道状态信息）建立映射。为保证系统能够把手枪和外形、材质相近的日常物品区分开，训练素材包含塑料手枪、金属水杯、真金属手枪以及手机的采集记录。 训练完成后，WiFireNet 仅依靠 Wi‑Fi 信道状态信息就可以检测隐藏手枪，但精度存在波动。在受控实验环境中，狭小室内空间最多同时追踪四名移动人员，这套系统检测手枪的平均精确率为 72.5%。但如果提出更严格的定位要求，例如精准定位武器在携带者身上的具体位置，精确率会下降至 53.8%。当遇到陌生、未经过测试的室内布局时，神经网络识别效果也会明显变差。 该系统目前仍处于实验阶段，研究团队规划了后续优化路线。原型机采用经过改造的老旧 1999 年 IEEE 802.11a 无线标准来验证原理。下一阶段将采用 Wi‑Fi 7、Wi‑Fi 8 现代无线网络，获取分辨率更高的信道状态信息，提升检测性能。研究团队将项目开源，放出代码、模型和数据集，推动该领域后续研究。 IT之家注意到，基于 Wi‑Fi 感知的监控技术正受到越来越多关注，其无需复杂设备与部署。但批评者认为，这项技术可以广泛部署，同时缺少对应的监管框架，会带来严重的隐私隐患。

_all_articles.title: 豆包刘星回应“国内超一半算力在造爽剧”：字节总算力中，只有约 10% 用于视频生成模型的训练和推理

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 19 日消息，近日，“国内超一半算力在造爽剧”的话题引发关注。 IT之家注意到，据中文在线在一份“投资者关系活动记录表”中披露，国内 AI Token 消耗 55% 烧在短剧和视频生成，24% 烧在电商广告，真正用于研发的只有 15%。AI 短剧与视频生成的 Token 消耗量已达到软件开发的两倍以上，成为整个 Token 经济学中第一大核心消耗场景。 豆包公关负责人刘星今日发文表示，这个算力数据有些不靠谱， 就字节来说，我们公司的总算力中，只有约 10%，用于视频生成模型的训练和推理 。 相关阅读： 《 AI 短剧爆火：制作成本仅为真人剧 1/10，平均每 36 秒诞生 1 部 》 《 广电总局：全国微短剧用户已超 8 亿，2025 年市场规模突破千亿元 》

_all_articles.title_original: 消息称索尼第一方游戏《羊蹄山之魂》销量约 540 万份，收入达 4.07 亿美元
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，市场分析机构 Alinea Analytics 现已公布索尼第一方游戏《羊蹄山之魂》的销售数据估算。本作目前销量约为 540 万份，收入 4.07 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 27.28 亿元人民币） 左右。作为参考，前作《对马岛之魂》在发售后的相同阶段，累计收入约为 4.18 亿美元 （现汇率约合 28.02 亿元人民币） ，销量估计接近 700 万份。 Rhys Elliott 补充道，两款作品所处的市场环境也存在明显差异。《对马岛之魂》生命周期中，市面上约有 1.17 亿台 PS4 和 1000 万台 PS5，而《羊蹄山之魂》仅登陆 PS5，而 PS5 装机量不到 1 亿台。 同时，《羊蹄山之魂》的标准版定价为 70 美元 （现汇率约合 469.2 元人民币） ，高于前作的 60 美元 （现汇率约合 402.2 元人民币） ，因此两款游戏的收入差距并不明显。 尽管销量增速可能不及前作，但 Alinea Analytics 认为《羊蹄山之魂》的整体表现依然强劲，本作在商业层面上并非失败。

_all_articles.title: 陈立武：美国政府不会干预英特尔经营，公司重组工作已完成 80%
_all_articles.title_original: 陈立武：美国政府不会干预英特尔经营，公司重组工作已完成 80%
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，英特尔首席执行官陈立武（Lip-Bu Tan）在接受《日经新闻》专访时表示，美国总统唐纳德・特朗普的政府没有任何政策打算借助所持英特尔少数股权干预这家芯片厂商的经营战略。 陈立武本月早些时候在东京称：“他们没有相关政策，对公司治理也不具备任何影响力。”他强调英特尔保持“独立”，有权基于自身最大利益自主决策。 美国政府去年将此前划拨的联邦资助转为 89 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 596.56 亿元人民币） 投资，由此获得英特尔 9.9% 股份；在 8 月的二次增发后，持股被稀释至约 8.2%。 这家深陷困境的美国芯片企业正努力重建先进半导体制造领域的地位。在芯片代工赛道，其已经落后于台积电；在 AI 芯片领域，市场份额也被英伟达等美国竞争对手蚕食。 在前任 CEO 帕特・基辛格（Pat Gelsinger）任期内，英特尔启动了宏大的投资计划发力芯片代工业务，投入数十亿美元扩充产能。但高昂的重组成本导致公司 2024 年第三季度净亏损 166 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1,112.68 亿元人民币） ，基辛格于同年 12 月辞职。 去年 8 月，特朗普政府出手购入 4.333 亿股英特尔被动股权，不占有董事会席位。这笔投资的初衷，是支持英特尔在美国本土扩建先进芯片制造产能。 陈立武表示，美国政府的支持有助于英特尔投入长期资本，打造具备竞争力的晶圆代工业务。他以台积电举例，称台积电耗费 10 至 20 年时间，才成长为全球顶尖代工厂。 “站在代工厂的角度，英特尔必须着眼长期视角，强有力的政府支持至关重要。”他补充，如果运营得当，代工业务有望成为增长引擎，但“这需要时间”。 芯片厂商需要在多年间持续投入数百亿资本开支，建设工厂并迭代越来越精密的制造工艺。 英特尔的重组计划还获得了其他资金助力：日本软银集团与竞争对手英伟达合计投资约 70 亿美元 （现汇率约合 469.2 亿元人民币） ，并获得对应股权。 陈立武对两家投资方表达感谢，同时表示这笔投资对投资方而言同样具备财务收益，他们有望“赚取丰厚利润”，实现 5 至 6 倍回报。英特尔当前股价约每股 100 美元 （现汇率约合 670.3 元人民币） ，相比陈立武 2025 年 3 月上任时，股价大约翻了四倍。 陈立武称英特尔的重组工作已完成 80%，并把 AI 先进芯片封装、专用集成电路（ASIC）视作其他潜在增长赛道 。就任 CEO 之后，他更换了大部分高管团队，招揽顶尖人才，例如韩国存储芯片大厂 SK 海力士前 CEO 李锡熙（Seok-Hee Lee），该企业同样凭借先进存储芯片搭上 AI 浪潮。 马来西亚华裔出身的陈立武拥有麻省理工学院工程学位，此前长期担任硅谷芯片设计工具厂商 Cadence Design Systems 的首席执行官。当被问及中国半导体产业带来的竞争威胁时，这位 66 岁的高管态度相对审慎，他表示，无论企业来自美国还是中国，“各自都有不同优势与短板，更重要的是怎样对消费者、企业用户最有利”，同时他也留意到“地缘政治限制”带来的敏感性。 被问到中国芯片实力能否在 5 至 10 年内追上美国时，陈立武给出简短评价：“就现在来看，差距并没有那么大。”

_all_articles.title: 微软发布法律版 Copilot：律师的 AI 新同事，整合审查合同等超 20 项技能
_all_articles.title_original: 微软发布法律版 Copilot：律师的 AI 新同事，整合审查合同等超 20 项技能
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，微软副董事长兼总裁布拉德 · 史密斯（Brad Smith）昨日（10 月 16 日）发布推文， 宣布微软推出 Copilot for Legal，为全球商用客户提供超过 20 项面向法律工作的专用 AI Skills（技能）。 这些专用 Skills 围绕着法律工作专门构建，以法律插件形式集成到 Copilot 中。每项技能都针对一个具体法律任务，例如起草合同、审查协议、追踪义务或整理案件时间线。IT之家附上相关截图如下： 在官方博文中，微软表示 Microsoft 365 Copilot 已整合起草、审查合同，义务追踪、整理案例等 AI Skills 任务，主要在 Word 桌面版和跨应用智能工作区 Cowork 中使用。 在 Word 中，Copilot 可依据企业预设的审查规则（playbook）审阅合同，识别需要关注的条款，并以“修订模式”提出修改建议；还能调用 SharePoint 中的核准模板或历史协议，生成新的合同草稿和法律备忘录。用户可逐项审核修改内容，最终决定是否采纳。 Cowork 则面向更复杂的多步骤工作流，可跨合同、邮件、会议记录和文件提取关键义务、期限与触发条件，比较不同协议条款，建立案件时间线，或将会议内容整理为正式会议纪要和决议。 微软还同步推出由法律科技公司构建的插件，合作方包括 Bloomberg Law、Thomson Reuters HighQ、DocuSign、Harvey、Relativity、iManage、NetDocuments 等，覆盖法律检索、文档管理、电子签署、电子取证和交易管理等场景。相关插件将通过微软插件注册表逐步上线，实际可用性会因地区、授权和管理员设置而异。 微软强调，该工具定位为法律专业人员的辅助，而非替代法律判断；AI 生成的引用、结论和修订建议仍需人工核验。企业需持有 Microsoft 365 Copilot 商用授权，并确认 Word 环境、支持语言及插件配置。 相关阅读： 《 微软 Word 上线“律政助手”智能体：能理解复杂法律文档、识别合同风险 》

_all_articles.title: Jev-as-a-Judge for RAG Claim Verification: Confidence-Gated Cascading Between a Non-Generative Verifier and a Frontier LLM
_all_articles.title_original: Jev-as-a-Judge for RAG Claim Verification: Confidence-Gated Cascading Between a Non-Generative Verifier and a Frontier LLM
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.20634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation asks one question at volume: does this evidence support this claim? The answer is one bit, yet most pipelines obtain it from a text generator and pay generation prices for the prose wrapped around it. We compare a non-generative decision model, which returns a typed value from a declared enumeration together with a native probability and no text, against a frontier LLM configured as an engineer would deploy it for binary classification. Both answer the same 495 human-labelled claims from LLM-AggreFact, so every comparison is within-item. We report three things. First, the two systems are statistically indistinguishable on the metric this task is conventionally scored by, a paired difference of -0.56 points, Jev minus Astra, at a 187-fold cost difference. Second, that tie carries almost no information about deployment: the systems disagree on 15.2% of claims, and the cheaper one admits 23.2% of the claims annotators marked unsupported against the frontier model's 14.1%. A component whose job is to catch unsupported claims should be judged on that rate, and the conventional headline hides it. Third, because the errors differ they compose: routing the claims the cheap model is confident about and escalating the rest reaches 74.10 at USD 2.92 per thousand claims against 73.83 at USD 8.93, with the threshold chosen out of fold. But a matched random-escalation control at in-sample thresholds, spending the same budget by coin flip, does as well, so what buys the saving is the escalation share and not the probability that picks what to escalate. Measured against the cheap model it is built from, the cascade costs 61-fold more for 0.83 points, 95% CI [-3.36, 4.86], and it is the more permissive guard of the two. Equal accuracy conceals unequal errors. All predictions, prompts, pricing and code are released.

_all_articles.title: Gemini Hacked Three Companies in First Known Breakout by Google’s AI
_all_articles.title_original: Gemini Hacked Three Companies in First Known Breakout by Google’s AI
_all_articles.summary: Gemini Hacked Three Companies in First Known Breakout by Google’s AI Gemini finally caught up on Felony Bench ! The hacks, which the company confirmed on Friday, occurred in May as part of a test run by the company Irregular, which was also involved in similar incidents disclosed by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. In one of the cases, the model guessed passwords until it gained access to a protected system. In the other two cases, the model found credentials in a public repository that allowed it to then access protected systems. In each case, the model ended the intrusion after determining it had accessed a real company’s systems, Google said. Gemini is apparently less determined than other models, and decided not to keep going. Google knew about these in July, but chose not to disclose them until the WSJ reached out, presumably based on a tip. Google said it didn’t consider the hacks to warrant public disclosure—because its model didn’t cause harm to the companies and ended each intrusion immediately upon determining it had hacked a real company rather than a simulated one. _all_articles.title: The contagion of fear
_all_articles.title_original: The contagion of fear
_all_articles.summary: The contagion of fear Bryan Cantrill responds to the tweet by former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon confirming that many Anthropic researchers believe AI "could kill us all by the end of the decade". Bryan shares a story of his own youthful mistakes causing unjustified panic among less technical peers, and warns against doing the same: These ghoulish claims strike brazenly at the hearth, and given the obvious importance of AI, it is unsurprising that they have leapt into the mainstream, with people asking the natural question: how would that happen? The answers always rely on hand-wavy extrapolation into the future; for example, Jacob Coxon cites "hacking critical infrastructure" and "extinction-level bioweapons" without further elaboration. But Coxon is not an expert on critical infrastructure, nor on bioweapons — nor, for that matter, on extinction. [...] That said, we should not expect the public to understand LLMs, critical infrastructure, bioweapons, extinction biology, etc. — that burden must lie with those making the claim. The lesson that I learned (shamefully) decades ago is that domain experts, by way of their expertise, implicitly hold the public’s trust — and we must not abuse it. It is incumbent upon us to be circumspect in our claims — and maximally so when raising the alarm. Bryan talked about his doubts about the bioweapons concerns in the recent episode of Oxide and Friends that I joined. You can hear more of his thoughts on that starting at 51m44s in that episode. Here's 57m04s : I really think we need to be careful because it's so easy to be overcome with fear when we kind of make up these... it can give you biological weapons. Like, how? I mean, can we please have a biologist weigh in on this? Or can we have like someone who's got experience with bioweapons? [...] The bioweapon thing just gets under my fingernails because it leaves so much to the imagination that we insert with fear. Via Lobste.rs Tags: ai , anthropic , bryan-cantrill , ai-ethics

_all_articles.title: UniGuard: Multi-View Guardrail Learning for Cross-Interface Safety Generalization
_all_articles.title_original: UniGuard: Multi-View Guardrail Learning for Cross-Interface Safety Generalization
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Guardrail models are increasingly used as safety layers for LLMs and agentic systems, but most are trained on fixed prompt or response interfaces and become unreliable when the same safety case appears as a conversation, agent trajectory, multi-agent trace, or policy-conditioned input. We propose UniGuard, a training framework that learns interface-invariant safety representations from multiple semantically aligned views of the same safety case. We also construct the UniGuard-FT dataset by transforming 1,000 public safety cases into prompt, response, multi-turn conversation, agent-trace, and multi-agent-trace views, and train UniGuard-0.6B with classification, supervised contrastive learning, and asymmetric confidence calibration losses. Across unseen-interface benchmarks ATBench, PolicyGuardBench, and DynaBench, UniGuard-0.6B improves over its pretrained guardrail by 45.12 F1 points on average and reduces expected calibration error by 35.41 points, while remaining competitive with much larger guardrails such as Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and GPT-5.2 - despite being a 0.6B model and trained only with synthetic data.

_all_articles.title: GRAM: Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging via Subspace Alignment
_all_articles.title_original: GRAM: Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging via Subspace Alignment
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Merging different models into a single model is highly desirable for multi-task deployment, particularly in regulated domains like healthcare. In such settings, models are often locally fine-tuned due to strict data privacy policies, necessitating that aggregation operates exclusively on the fine-tuned weights. Existing methods apply a uniform merge across all tasks, ignoring the geometric relationships among their learned subspaces. When task updates occupy misaligned subspaces, projecting them onto a shared low-rank basis discards task-relevant directions, a failure mode named \emph{subspace interference}. Through this study, we show that the per-task projection error of a merged model is governed by the principal-angle alignment between each task and the shared subspace, so that grouping geometrically compatible tasks provably reduces this error within each group. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging (GRAM)}, which uses the principal-angle geometry of task vectors to decide which tasks should be merged together and then performs a standard SVD-based merge within each coalition; the pipeline requires only the fine-tuned weights at merge time. With only one additional model ($\nK{=}2$), GRAM significantly mitigates subspace interference and consistently outperforms prior merging methods across language understanding (GLUE with Flan-T5), 8-task CLIP vision, and medical instruction tuning (Qwen2-7B-Instruct with four English/Chinese medical LoRAs).

_all_articles.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
_all_articles.title_original: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. Using SIM-UT, we evaluated three real-world WhatsApp-based health chatbots: a respiratory screening programme in India, a hearing health support programme in South Africa, and a diabetes and lifestyle coaching agent in Kenya. We compared a medically fine-tuned open model (MedGemma) against general-purpose frontier models (ChatGPT and Claude) across 5,000+ multilingual simulated conversation turns grounded in the personas, constraints, and communication patterns of the real user populations, over 2-4 iterative rounds. A key failure mode emerged in both model families: de-escalation risk. The agents initially identified medical emergencies correctly, but when the user minimised the symptoms without introducing new clinical information, they de-escalated, exhibiting clinically dangerous sycophancy, for example agreeing that vaginal bleeding in pregnancy was "not a problem" or that decreased fetal movements at 32 weeks "can be normal". We recommend user simulation-based behavioural evaluation, grounded in real user context and covering adversarial and edge cases, as standard practice for triage chatbots in production, so that safeguards can be added before deployment or in subsequent iterations.

_all_articles.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
_all_articles.title_original: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and strong cross-architecture generalization of OWP. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, OWP generalizes effectively to VideoLLaMA2-AV, improving performance by 4.6 and 3.9 points on the same benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZiiJianLiu/Omni-Woodpecker

_all_articles.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
_all_articles.title_original: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results both during evolution and after task assembly. Using this framework, we construct DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories spanning diverse domains and output formats, to train DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B. DataPraxis-27B achieves 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or surpassing frontier models such as GLM-5.2. DataPraxis-5K is available at huggingface.co/datasets/stargazerhust/DataPraxis-5k

_all_articles.title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
_all_articles.title_original: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.

_all_articles.title: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
_all_articles.title_original: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A typed decision maps evidence, a question and a fixed set of options to a probability for every option, computed in one forward pass, by reading a language model's logits or a small head over its hidden states, instead of generating and parsing text. The commercial system Jev popularised this System~1 interface, and open reproductions have followed. We report two uses of the pattern. \emph{Part I} describes an in-house System~1 judge that triages about 148K agentic coding session records for a training corpus. It replaces a frontier LLM judge that cost on the order of \$1,000 per pass and whose stored labels matched a fresh two-judge consensus on only 26.9\% of the sessions where the two judges agreed; a self-hosted frozen backbone with a rank-16 LoRA adapter and a pointer head answers three typed questions in one forward pass, judges 1,000 sessions in about three minutes of one GPU, about \$0.06 at a reference rate and roughly 1\% of the frontier judge's cost, and keeps every session inside the organisation. \emph{Part II} asks whether a readout that adds no parameters can be competitive and whether training one helps. Applying the public Eikos recipe and corpus of about 25K decisions to three further backbones (1B, 2B and 35B), we read the frozen output layer of a LoRA-adapted decoder. On the 111 public hard items of JevBench our single-seed 35B, developed with those items in view, scores 79.3\%, not significantly different from the commercial reference (73.0\%, unadjusted $p=0.12$) and ahead of five open systems after Holm--Bonferroni correction; our 2B is ahead of all four kev checkpoints on the leaderboard. A single-seed ablation finds no detectable benefit from training the 26 letter rows of the output layer, and a retrain on a later corpus release moves the 2B's hard-tier accuracy by 11.7 points, which shows how little small evaluations resolve.

_all_articles.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
_all_articles.title_original: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

_all_articles.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
_all_articles.title_original: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propose and execute new experiments. Furthermore, each result should shape what the team tries next. We therefore ask how AI researchers with different scientific backgrounds can build on one another's findings and sustain progress under a limited experimental budget. To address these challenges, we build a team of persistent AI researchers, each grounded in a different discipline, who keep private research histories, share experimental evidence, and receive research opportunities through adaptive allocation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this design by deploying the team to search for linear attention architectures, where it outperforms GDN2 at 1.3B scale on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and synthetic and real-world retrieval tasks. In controlled comparisons, removing any single organizational component from our design yields markedly weaker discoveries: without disciplinary backgrounds, the search plateaus early; without private histories, researchers make less progress despite identical shared evidence; and uniform selection falls short of adaptive allocation within the same budget. These results suggest that sustained autonomous discovery depends not only on stronger agents, but also on who explores, what they remember, and how research effort is allocated.

_all_articles.title: Combating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Domain Adaptation via Knowledge Recasting
_all_articles.title_original: Combating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Domain Adaptation via Knowledge Recasting
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting language models to new domains during post-training risks degrading previously acquired capabilities, a phenomenon commonly known as catastrophic forgetting. Existing mitigation methods largely treat forgetting as a consequence of excessive model drift. They therefore constrain updates by preserving old outputs, replaying old data, or regularizing changes to parameters and representations so that the updated model remains close to its previous state. We take a different view: Rather than pulling the updated model back toward its old state, we translate the new domain into the model's pre-existing knowledge space, making unfamiliar knowledge learnable through familiar procedures. Therefore, we propose Skill Schema Transport (SST), a post-training framework that transports new knowledge into the model's existing skill space. SST abstracts each example type into a skill schema, preserving its essential operations, dependencies, and verification steps while removing domain-specific surface forms. By recasting new examples as instances of reusable procedures, SST turns knowledge update from trajectory memorization into procedural reuse. In continual domain adaptation settings, SST consistently reduces forgetting while improving generalization to related tasks. Across two 3B instruction-tuned backbones, SST improves average final performance on streamed domains by 2.53 to 5.75 points over sequential post-training. It also lowers max-drop forgetting in all evaluated settings, with the largest reduction from 42.41 to 7.10 points on the Qwen-3B MATH stream, while substantially recovering the OOD degradation induced by sequential updates.

_all_articles.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
_all_articles.title_original: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

_all_articles.title: Monte Carlo Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
_all_articles.title_original: Monte Carlo Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most KV-cache eviction methods ask, in effect, which memory appeared important while reading the prompt? We instead ask, which memory will matter while answering? Since decoding queries are unavailable at eviction time, prior future-aware methods rely on pseudo-responses or synthetic future-query estimates. We cast fixed-budget future-aware eviction as distributional estimation over plausible model-conditional query trajectories and introduce LORE-KV (Lookahead Output-perturbation with Reliability-weighted Ensembles for Key-Value caches), a training-free method that samples short autoregressive continuations from the frozen target model and uses their response-side query states to estimate prompt-token utility. Tokens are scored by projected leave-one-out attention-output deletion cost and aggregated across sampled futures with optional trajectory weighting. The temporary continuations are discarded before final decoding, requiring no auxiliary model or training. Ablations isolate the mechanism: at B=128, a single response-side continuation recovers about 89% of the gain over the prompt-window control, while additional futures provide smaller improvements. At B=128, LORE-KV raises the LongBench average on Qwen2.5-14B from 45.49 to 48.24 (+2.75) and the 16K RULER average on Mistral-7B from 45.20 to 51.05 (+5.85). Gains diminish at larger cache budgets and coexist with task-level regressions. LORE-KV incurs 1.46-2.77x AnDPro's per-sample wall-clock time as a one-time compression overhead across six dense and hybrid-attention backbones.

_all_articles.title: Learning from the Gap Between Pass@K and Pass@1
_all_articles.title_original: Learning from the Gap Between Pass@K and Pass@1
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.35793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). An exact verifier can also support test-time scaling by selecting a passing response from multiple samples, while other deployments use beam search, adaptive sampling, or tools. We study single-sample decoding, where each query receives one response without search, to ask whether search-exposed behavior can be absorbed into the model. Existing verified-response post-training recipes do not generally distinguish problems already solved on the first decode from failures recovered within K samples. Under a fixed budget, this can spend examples repeating behavior the deployed policy already has. We introduce GapFT, which selects training evidence by the source checkpoint's single-sample outcome and fine-tunes on the Pass@K-Pass@1 gap: problems the policy fails on one sample but solves within K samples. We match training examples, processed tokens, and optimizer steps while keeping the objective unchanged. GapFT fills the matched budget with recovered failures and uses an exact decomposition to distinguish corrections of recovered and missed failures from regressions on first-decode successes. On LogiQA 2.0 and ReClor with Llama-3.1-8B, GapFT improves Pass@1 by 14.4 and 13.9 points over the source model, outperforms budget-matched uniform verified RFT at the same learning rate, and matches fine-tuning on the full verified pool using one third of the data. A single decode matches the source model's verifier-selected Pass@4 accuracy. A randomized control attributes gains to covering distinct failures, and our analysis relates available gains to transferable failure support. A three-seed Qwen2.5-7B replication retains positive gains over uniform RFT on both logic tasks.

_all_articles.title: Hunyuan-A13B Technical Report
_all_articles.title_original: Hunyuan-A13B Technical Report
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.27284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Hunyuan-A13B, an open-source large language model based on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. It contains 80 billion total parameters but activates only 13 billion during inference, balancing model capability, computational efficiency, and deployment cost. The model is pretrained on a rigorously filtered 20T-token corpus with enhanced STEM data curation, improving factual reliability and reasoning ability. High-quality supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning further enhance its overall performance. Hunyuan-A13B also introduces a dual-mode Chain-of-Thought framework that adapts reasoning depth to task complexity: fast thinking for routine queries and slow thinking for complex, multi-step problems. Evaluations show competitive performance across mathematics, science, programming, general language understanding, and agent tasks, often approaching that of much larger models. Its high inference throughput makes it suitable for latency-sensitive applications. We release Hunyuan-A13B to support open research and practical LLM deployment.

_all_articles.title: Stable Geometry with Divergent Task Evidence for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Compression
_all_articles.title_original: Stable Geometry with Divergent Task Evidence for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Compression
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.27332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long horizon agents accumulate growing interaction histories that increase context and inference costs. We find that geometric redundancy alone is an insufficient criterion for safe compression. Although agent histories exhibit strong low dimensional structure, similar global geometry can preserve very different amounts of task evidence. At identical retained block counts, evidence aware selection raises next action Top 3 retention from 0.31 to 0.69, while centroid similarity remains 0.98. Controlled replacement further shows that action related information can be substantially altered while global geometric measures remain nearly unchanged. Motivated by this gap between geometry and evidence, we introduce Geometry Guided Evidence Preserving Memory (GEM), a training free compressor that protects task and execution evidence before using geometric residuals to complete coverage. GEM reduces mean combined token usage from 2.69M to 2.11M per task, a 21.4% reduction, while maintaining comparable task reward. Our results show that efficient agent history compression should optimize for preserved task evidence rather than geometric coverage alone.

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，当地时间 22 日，据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士消息称，中国 AI 初创企业 DeepSeek 完成第二轮私募融资，筹资 150 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,003.23 亿元人民币） 。投资者认购意愿强烈，推动融资规模扩大至接近最初目标的两倍，为潜在上市计划提供了资金支持。 知情人士称，DeepSeek 正加快推进首次公开募股（IPO），争取明年初在上海上市。如果上市顺利，DeepSeek 有望先于 OpenAI、月之暗面登陆资本市场。 据参与融资的知情人士透露，本轮融资完成前，DeepSeek 估值约为 740 亿美元 （现汇率约合 4,949.29 亿元人民币） 。 宁德时代和腾讯 继上一轮投资后，再次参与注资。 部分知情人士称，DeepSeek 本轮融资从 7 月持续至 10 月，耗时超过近期其他 AI 企业的融资项目。随着谈判推进，更多投资者陆续加入。 此前消息称，砺思资本、拾象资本等现有股东也在本轮融资中追加投资。 据知情人士透露，新加入的投资者包括专注于半导体行业的私募股权投资机构石溪资本。 获得联想集团支持的君联资本 、汽车制造商吉利，也同样参与了投资。 知情人士称，DeepSeek 聘请中信证券担任 IPO 顾问，并于 9 月任命曾从事风险投资的严文韬为 CFO。 DeepSeek 筹集巨额资金之际，部分投资者对 AI 企业的盈利前景愈发审慎，开始质疑大规模资本投入能否带来持续盈利，以及 AI 企业不断上涨的估值是否合理。 据知情人士透露，DeepSeek 创始人梁文锋 9 月向投资者披露，公司按当前收入水平计算的年化收入规模达到 10 亿美元 （现汇率约合 66.88 亿元人民币） 。年化收入是衡量订阅制服务经营表现的重要指标。 相关阅读： 《 向硅谷巨头发起挑战，消息称 DeepSeek 最新一轮融资筹集近千亿元 》

_all_articles.title_original: 英伟达 Vera CPU 获 AI 初创公司 Modal 订单，杀入英特尔、AMD 主场
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 20 日消息，据路透社报道，英伟达拿下又一家高速成长 AI 初创企业的中央处理器订单。在此之前，这家企业完全依赖英特尔与 AMD 的芯片。这是一个早期信号，说明英伟达进军这个长期由两大对手把持市场的战略已经初见成效。 云算力初创公司 Modal 面向 AI 开发者提供算力租赁服务。该公司表示，计划首次采用英伟达全新 Vera 中央处理器来托管智能体（AI agents），也就是能够替人类执行长周期任务的 AI 系统。在此之前，Modal 这类业务仅在英特尔和 AMD 芯片上运行。 Modal 上周完成了由 Accel 领投的 7.5 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 50.2 亿元人民币） 融资，投后估值达 157.5 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1,054.25 亿元人民币） 。公司称预计下一年营收有望达到 10 亿美元 （现汇率约合 66.94 亿元人民币） 。Modal 表示其服务使用量增长两倍，同比营收增幅超过 15 倍。 Modal 当地时间周一称，早期测试显示这款英伟达新芯片能让 AI 智能体的任务处理吞吐量提升一倍，因此决定首次接入英伟达芯片方案，这需要 Modal 对底层软件进行深度改造。 不过首席执行官埃里克・伯恩哈德松（Erik Bernhardsson）特意强调，公司并不会放弃现有供应商。Modal 表示会采用混合算力集群，英伟达芯片将与当前的英特尔、AMD 设备并行部署，把不同任务调度到最适配的硬件上。 伯恩哈德松介绍，本次测试的对标对象是市面上已量产的英特尔、AMD 芯片。英伟达的这两家竞品厂商都在研发新一代产品，有望缩小与英伟达之间的性能差距。 “等新品上市，我们会进行测试。”他补充道，混合硬件架构意味着公司“随时可以部署性能最优的硬件”。 英伟达向投资者透露，本财年 Vera 芯片销售额目标至少 200 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1,338.73 亿元人民币） 。这是英伟达打入这个规模约 2,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1.34 万亿元人民币） 市场的开局。英伟达此前曾表示，OpenAI、Anthropic、甲骨文以及 Perplexity 这类 AI 初创企业也计划采用该芯片。

_all_articles.title: Causal Syntax Circuits in CodeLMs: Budget and Probe Decide What Looks Localised
_all_articles.title_original: Causal Syntax Circuits in CodeLMs: Budget and Probe Decide What Looks Localised
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.20683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Code models write Python when the prompt does not say which language to use. We ask a mechanistic question about that habit: is it produced by a small, findable group of components inside the model? We run one pipeline---mean ablation, activation patching, greedy circuit extraction, a random-control significance test, and activation steering---over 55 model-language settings spanning ten open code models (five base and five instruction-tuned), three target languages (Rust, C#, PHP), two prompt suites, and two component budgets. We report five findings. First, the preference is large, grows with model size, and survives instruction tuning: it is larger on every instruction-tuned checkpoint than on its base version, by 12% on average. Second, its measured size is mostly a property of the probe; replacing our aligned prompts with XLCoST parallel functions takes the same measurement on the same models from about 1.6 to about 0.01. Third, whether the preference looks localised depends on how many components the search may keep: with a budget of 12, 1 of 15 settings yields a circuit that beats size-matched random controls after multiple-comparison correction, and with a budget of 40, 6 of 15 do. Fourth, interventions that a smaller-budget study reports as uniformly failing do sometimes succeed: patching makes a Python prompt prefer target syntax in 2 of 45 settings, and steering changes the most likely next token in 9 of 45. Fifth, every circuit whose effect is significant but points away from the target language comes from a setting where circuit extraction failed, which makes such results a diagnostic rather than a phenomenon. The practical lesson is that a claim about whether a behaviour is localised can turn on analysis choices that papers rarely report. We release the full grid so those choices can be varied.

_all_articles.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
_all_articles.title_original: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.20951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models answer typed questions about an input with one probability per option, computed in a single forward pass without generating text. Like the fast System 1 of dual-process theory, they answer at once, but their depth is fixed at training time, so they spend the same computation on easy and hard questions. Models that reason in generated text can think longer, but they pay for every extra step in decoded tokens. We present LEV, a decision model that thinks deeper by rerunning its layers in a loop instead of generating tokens. LEV builds on a language model pretrained as a loop, reads the options after every loop step and trains all steps jointly, so one checkpoint can answer at any depth. On three looped backbones, accuracy rises with depth on the same weights, mostly on hard questions, and a 2.6B LEV goes from 63.2% at depth one to 76.2% at depth four on JevBench. On-demand depth, set per question by a small stopper with a threshold fitted on unlabelled requests, saves 15% to 24% of the computation at a cost of under one accuracy point, level with or slightly above a fixed mix of depths. On a locked test set, the 1.4B and 3B models are 5.4 to 8.8 points more accurate than dense (non-looped) models and cascades of the same latency below 50 ms.

_all_articles.title: Backpropagating Verifier Rewards Through Continuous Flow Language Models
_all_articles.title_original: Backpropagating Verifier Rewards Through Continuous Flow Language Models
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.19080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the reasoning of autoregressive and discrete-diffusion language models. Language models that generate continuous token embeddings are emerging as a strong alternative, but RL post-training for them remains understudied. We propose \method{}, a post-training framework for continuous flow language models. Such a model denoises token embeddings over multiple steps and decodes them into discrete tokens only at the last step. To obtain pathwise gradients, which backpropagate through continuous actions and have much lower variance than REINFORCE, we introduce a critic that estimates the value of intermediate token embeddings, bypassing the non-differentiable decoding step. The critic must also keep track of the value function as the policy changes; to this end, we design a critic that predicts a value from every token representation and improves policy optimization. Across four reasoning tasks, \method{} reliably improves a continuous flow language model through RL post-training and outperforms baseline methods of the same type.

_all_articles.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
_all_articles.title_original: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns. Yet forcing a model to imitate externally provided trajectories may also interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining, limiting generalization beyond the training distribution. Recent dynamic SFT methods mitigate this issue by reweighting token-level supervision according to model-side signals such as predictive probability, prior support, or distributional compatibility. However, model compatibility is not equivalent to learning value: a token that is weakly supported by the current model may either be an undesirable mismatch or precisely the task-specific decision that the demonstration is intended to teach. We propose CIG-SFT, an information-theoretic framework that estimates the task-conditioned information carried by each demonstrated token. Under teacher forcing, we compare the token likelihood from a frozen reference model with and without access to the task input while keeping the gold solution prefix fixed. The resulting conditional information gain quantifies how much the task itself reduces uncertainty about the demonstrated decision. We then convert this information into a KL-regularized projection of the current policy and derive an equivalent scalar-weighted SFT objective whose logit gradient exactly matches that of the projected target. Across mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, CIG-SFT consistently outperforms standard SFT and recent adaptive fine-tuning baselines, with particularly strong improvements in generalization to challenging evaluation distributions, while requiring neither additional training data nor online rollouts.

_all_articles.title_original: 不满 Mistral 表现，德国搜索引擎 Ecosia 押注中国开源 AI 模型
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，据《政治报》前天报道，德国搜索引擎 Ecosia 最近选择放弃法国 AI 模型 Mistral，转而选择中国开源 AI 模型。 Ecosia 创始人兼 CEO 克里斯蒂安 · 克罗尔接受采访时表示：“我们对 Mistral 的质量感到失望，该模型如今已落后竞争对手一整年。” 今年 5 月，Ecosia 宣布放弃美国 OpenAI 方案，将 AI 服务供应商切换为 Mistral。据克罗尔所述，这次合作并不算顺利，公司经常遇到服务器过载等技术问题。 IT之家从原报道获悉，Ecosia 还担心 Mistral 是否符合环保目标。法国能源结构中核电占比较高，且该公司对 Mistral 是否能保持中立表示质疑。克罗尔解释称：“Mistral 依赖国际投资者资金，因此并不算真正意义上的主权企业。” 这名 CEO 还认为， 中国积极推动开源大模型发展 ， 对欧洲来说是一大机遇 。尽管欧洲错过了 AI 模型发展第一阶段，但现在他们可以利用日益强大的开源模型，而不必投入数十亿美元自行训练前沿 AI。 所以 Ecosia 如今选择与 Melious 合作，使用中国的 Qwen、GLM 和 Kimi 模型。这让他们的成本降低一半，还获得了性能提升。
