_all_articles.title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
_all_articles.title_original: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. A unified schema-conditioned language--symbol interface, trained offline with supervised fine-tuning, connects text environments to the planning loop through observation-to-fact parsing and symbolic-action-to-command grounding. Experiments on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and Robotouille show that MemPlan improves task completion and step efficiency over language-only and PDDL-aware baselines, while substantially reducing online token cost compared with LLM-planning baselines such as ReAct. The same fine-tuned interface is also reused across TextWorld task types without task-specific fine-tuning. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/tewiSong/MemPlan.

_all_articles.title: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
_all_articles.title_original: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable feedback is essential for coding agents to develop programs for partial differential equations (PDEs). Yet evaluating these programs on new PDE problems often requires expensive reference computations, while fixed datasets restrict the range of experiments. We introduce Generator-Agent-Verifier (GAV), a scientific experimentation environment that makes new PDE problems verifiable by construction. The Generator learns a distribution of continuous reference solutions using data from numerical simulations or experimental measurements to represent a target physical regime. Using the method of manufactured solutions, it works backward from the generated reference solutions to construct matching PDE problems without a separate numerical solve. The Agent designs experiments, investigates failures, and iteratively improves its program. The Verifier evaluates candidate programs against the reference solutions and provides numerical feedback on accuracy and computational cost. This feedback can also guide the generation of new problems that probe the current program's weaknesses. We provide a theoretical analysis of evaluation reliability and guided development. Experiments on Navier-Stokes and Vlasov-Poisson-type equations across different data sources and regimes demonstrate the effectiveness of GAV. In particular, on the numerical Navier-Stokes task, GAV reduces the mean test error of three existing PDE agents by more than an order of magnitude relative to their original setups. Code is available at https://github.com/PotatoJnny/PDE-GAV.

_all_articles.title: CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer
_all_articles.title_original: CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-tokenizer logits distillation enables knowledge transfer across model families, allowing students to learn from stronger or more specialized teachers. However, differences in vocabulary and segmentation make teacher and student next-token distributions difficult to align. Existing logits-based methods are easy to integrate into standard distillation pipelines, but often rely on restrictive heuristics or tokenizer-pair-specific choices. They may restrict supervision to shared vocabulary subsets, require manually selecting different objectives for different tokenizer pairs, or match only the observed chunk and its complement rather than individual alternative continuations. We introduce Common-Support Distillation (CSD), a unified logits-based framework that constructs a shared support between the teacher and student at each aligned input chunk and matches the induced distributions with a single objective. For one-to-one alignments, CSD uses explicit common-token pairs as the shared support. For other alignments, it constructs a virtual support whose probabilities are computed using the autoregressive chain rule. A residual event captures probability mass outside the explicit support, ensuring that both induced distributions remain normalized. Across four teacher-student settings comprising Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma3-1B-PT students with Qwen and Phi teachers, CSD consistently achieves the highest average performance among the evaluated cross-tokenizer methods, outperforming the strongest alternative by up to 1.8 points and surpassing both continued pretraining and same-tokenizer distillation. For Llama-3.1-8B, CSD improves average accuracy over the strongest evaluated baseline by up to 4.2 points for the base student and 1.6 points for the instruction-tuned student.

_all_articles.title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?
_all_articles.title_original: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In case-based legal reasoning, legal professionals identify legally significant fact patterns in a new dispute and compare them with those of decided cases. In AI & Law, HYPO dimensions and CATO factors represent these patterns symbolically, organizing expert knowledge distilled from case narratives as explicit, structured, interpretable, and auditable legal concepts and relations that support case comparison, legal argument, and precedent-based reasoning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for legal tasks, yet their internal organization of legal knowledge remains difficult to trace. We investigate whether LLMs form internal representations corresponding to all 26 CATO factors. Two research questions examine linear decodability and sparse localization with sparse autoencoders. Experiments cover three open models, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-2 2B, supported by cross-model comparison and human audit of controlled natural-language passages. Results show that all 26 factors are linearly decodable in all three models. Single-feature sparse readouts cover the complete factor catalog, with best-layer test AUCs ranging from 0.86 to 1.00. Five selected features approach full-vector readout performance. We report 78 model-specific layer-feature coordinates, one for each factor in each model. Together, these results show that information corresponding to expert-defined legal factors can be read from the internal activations of LLMs processing legal narratives. By locating these readouts, our study connects legal language and the symbolic abstractions of HYPO and CATO to learned internal representations.

_all_articles.title: An Explicit Feedback Contract for Iterative ML-Agent Harnesses
_all_articles.title_original: An Explicit Feedback Contract for Iterative ML-Agent Harnesses
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterative ML agents develop models by editing code, running experiments, reading a validation score, and choosing what to try next. In current harnesses this loop is served by an exact validation score returned after every attempt, which leaves the validation split open to adaptive selection. In this work, we introduce an explicit feedback contract for ML-agent harnesses, which specifies what an agent may observe, when iteration should stop, and when the test split may be touched. The contract releases a validation score only when a submission clears a noise threshold computed from the paired standard error, so no margin has to be tuned. We ran experiments on click-through-rate prediction, learning to rank, and a control task with no signal to find. The control is the sharpest case, because the true gain there is zero by construction: an agent reading exact scores ended by reporting a gain of 0.0157, while under the contract it reported 0.0033. On both real tasks the contract narrows the validation-test gap, and test performance is slightly higher rather than lower. The largest difference is in when the agents stop. Exact feedback used its entire budget of thirty submissions on two of the three tasks, including the one where nothing can be learned, while the contract halted after four to twelve. A run that exhausts its budget is usually read as diligence. It is better read as a symptom: when the feedback channel is unbounded, noise keeps supplying improvements to chase.

_all_articles.title: The Data Differentiator Framework (DDF): Quantifying Marginal Data Value with Information-Theoretic and Game-Theoretic Measures in an Agentic Evaluation Pipeline (SDSAE)
_all_articles.title_original: The Data Differentiator Framework (DDF): Quantifying Marginal Data Value with Information-Theoretic and Game-Theoretic Measures in an Agentic Evaluation Pipeline (SDSAE)
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In data-rich enterprises the hard question is not whether a candidate dataset is good in isolation, but whether it adds information beyond what the organization already holds, and whether that increment is worth its price. We present the Data Differentiator Framework (DDF), a composite scoring method for candidate data assets that combines (i) a mutual-information-based redundancy penalty against the existing portfolio, (ii) a cost-normalized, significance-gated marginal utility score derived from an ablation study, and (iii) explicit governance inputs (trust, identity resolution quality, strategic weights) set by the business. The framework is executed by a staged pipeline, the Strategic Data Sourcing Agent Ecosystem (SDSAE), that short-circuits expensive model-retraining steps for assets failing governance or redundancy gates. Conceptually, the DDF extends the relevance-minus-redundancy principle of mRMR feature selection from the feature level to the asset level, and adds cost normalization, a statistical significance gate, and governance terms that per-sample valuation methods such as Data Shapley do not model. We validate the framework on the public credit-card fraud benchmark (284,807 transactions) with five constructed candidate assets spanning the redundancy spectrum. Only the genuinely differentiated asset passes the significance gate ($\Delta$AUC = +0.0029, DeLong $p = 1.4\times 10^{-9}$, Holm-corrected $p = 7.2\times 10^{-9}$) and receives an acquire recommendation (DDS = +0.663); the fully redundant asset scores lowest (DDS = -0.135). The recommendation is stable across 19 of 22 admissible strategic-weight configurations and across all decision thresholds in [0.15, 0.66]. We state clearly which quantities in the case study are computed from data and which are simulated governance inputs, and we discuss the design limits of a single-dataset evaluation.

_all_articles.title: EmbeddingGemma 2
_all_articles.title_original: EmbeddingGemma 2
_all_articles.summary: My comment on EmbeddingGemma 2 — Hacker News. I really appreciate that EmbeddingGemma 2 is under the Apache 2.0 license. For embedding models in particular, I don't think it makes sense to use a closed, proprietary, hosted-only model. Most applications of embedding models involve calculating thousands or even millions of embedding vectors and storing them for later comparison. If your model is proprietary, the vendor is likely someday going to decide to stop offering that model. They'll have a better model to replace it, but you still need to pay to re-calculate those millions of stored existing vectors. (In April 2024 OpenAI offered to "cover the financial cost of users re-embedding content with these new models" - https://openai.com/index/gpt-4-api-general-availability/ - but I don't think that's something we can rely on from every provider.) Notably, I don't want to host the model myself . I'd much rather pay a provider for a hosted model while knowing that if they ever stop hosting it I can run the open weights version myself - or find another vendor who can do that for me. Tags: google , ai , generative-ai , embeddings , gemma

_all_articles.title: Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
_all_articles.title_original: Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.10878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) efficiently transfers capabilities from a stronger teacher to a student language model through dense token-level supervision on student-generated rollouts and has shown promise on complex tasks such as mathematical reasoning. However, in multi-turn agentic tasks, student decisions shape subsequent observations, causing early errors to accumulate across turns. The resulting trajectories can drift away from the teacher's rollout distribution, making the teacher's token-level supervision less reliable or even counterproductive for OPD training. To address this issue, we introduce STI-OPD, a stochastic teacher intervention framework for multi-turn agentic OPD. During multi-turn interaction, STI-OPD uses teacher intervention guided by teacher-student policy discrepancy to replace the student's proposed action with a teacher-generated one to maximize the acquisition of reliable supervision. We further develop a stochastic intervention strategy, addressing the limitations of previous threshold-based or fixed-schedule approaches, that estimates policy discrepancy using KL divergence and maps it to an intervention probability. By sampling whether to intervene from this probability, STI-OPD adaptively balances teacher control with student exploration. To learn from the resulting mixed-policy trajectories, we introduce an Importance-Weighted Reverse KL objective that corrects the token sampling mismatch between teacher-generated responses and the student policy to preserve the original OPD objective. Across tool-integrated reasoning and long-horizon interaction, STI-OPD outperforms the strongest prior OPD baseline on every evaluated benchmark and student size. Ablations further show that both discrepancy-guided intervention and importance weighting contribute to these gains.

_all_articles.title: ShamAN-Q: Shampoo Augmented NanoQuant for Sub-1-bit LLM Weights
_all_articles.title_original: ShamAN-Q: Shampoo Augmented NanoQuant for Sub-1-bit LLM Weights
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.38521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce ShamAN-Q, a sub-1-bit post-training quantization method that extends NanoQuant by replacing each its diagonal reconstruction geometry with a tractable dense curvature metric, using a general paradigm popularized by the Shampoo optimizer. For each linear weight, ShamAN-Q fits a Kronecker product to the empirical Fisher information matrix of a small calibration set by Kullback--Leibler minimization, forming a Mahalanobis reconstruction loss from the result. The continuous ADMM updates from NanoQuant become solutions to Sylvester equations, while its discrete projection and deployment format remain unchanged. Because the curvature is local to a given set of weights, ShamAN-Q re-measures the input curvature statistic for each layer immediately before layer factorization, periodically refreshing all statistics on the partially quantized model. ShamAN-Q also redistributes the uniform rank from NanoQuant across layers at the same total number of bits. On Qwen3-Base, ShamAN-Q lowers WikiText-2 perplexity at $\approx$1 bpw from 27.56 to 22.96 (0.6B), 19.21 to 16.72 (1.7B), and 14.29 to 13.80 (4B) while matching or improving zero-shot accuracy on the Eleuther LM Evaluation Harness. On 0.6B, ShamAN-Q at $\approx$0.8 bpw matches the published perplexity of NanoQuant at $\approx$1.0 bpw.

_all_articles.title: BaseCamp --- An Agentic AI Framework for Automating DNA Sequencing Data Pipelines
_all_articles.title_original: BaseCamp --- An Agentic AI Framework for Automating DNA Sequencing Data Pipelines
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DNA sequencing pipelines, spanning quality control, alignment, variant calling, and annotation, are now reliably executed by workflow management systems that orchestrate established bioinformatics tools at scale. What remains manual is the decision layer surrounding that execution: selecting quality thresholds appropriate to a sample and platform, adjudicating borderline variant calls, diagnosing anomalies, and determining which findings warrant expert review. These decisions are repetitive, judgment-intensive, inconsistent across operators, and frequently undocumented. This paper introduces BaseCamp, a novel agentic AI framework for automating the decision layer of DNA sequencing pipelines. The framework decomposes the pipeline into six specialized AI agents, covering sample intake and quality control, alignment, variant calling, annotation, cross-stage monitoring, and reporting. Critically, BaseCamp agents do not perform sequence analysis: established tools execute alignment, calling, and annotation, while the agents select among them, configure them, interpret their output, and decide what follows. This confines language model reasoning to the judgment layer where it is reliable and preserves the reproducibility existing tooling guarantees. Agent reasoning is powered by a consortium of fine-tuned, domain-specialized large language models coordinated by a central reasoning LLM, executing locally so no sequencing data leaves the operating environment, under human-in-the-loop orchestration. Evaluation shows agent-generated configurations are concordant with expert practice, that an explicit filtering ledger renders inspectable what filtering otherwise removes without trace, and that cross-stage anomaly detection surfaces conditions execution monitoring misses. BaseCamp offers a generalizable blueprint for agentic automation of scientific data pipelines.

_all_articles.title: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment
_all_articles.title_original: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.19035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pluralistic alignment needs to accommodate diverse preferences under limited human feedback. Using AI simulators to label preference comparisons reduces annotation costs, but variation in simulation accuracy across individuals can leave some people's preferences poorly represented in training. We study how to allocate human feedback across people to construct training data for pluralistic alignment, and how this allocation affects the trained policy. To make this allocation explicit and controllable, we define a social welfare objective over individual supervision utilities that measure label quality. Each query's marginal welfare gain depends on its expected supervision improvement, the recipient's current utility, and application-designated priority. Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition (WAPA) uses auxiliary reference models to estimate query gains and individual utilities, then selects queries by estimated marginal welfare gain while updating recipient utilities. We prove exact optimality of the acquisition algorithm for the estimated welfare objective under a fixed query budget and model predictions. Experiments on six Roleplay collections and four OpinionQA regions demonstrate improved supervision and controllable allocation tradeoffs. Policy training on four Roleplay collections improves preference prediction for both seen and unseen individuals. When prioritizing a designated group and poorly represented individuals, acquiring human labels for 20% of comparisons recovers 75-86% of the average predictive utility gap between policies trained entirely on AI-generated labels and entirely on ground-truth labels.

_all_articles.title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
_all_articles.title_original: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a trader executes a large order, the relevant question is not \emph{what will the price be?} but \emph{what would the price have been had I not traded?} Market impact is thus a causal quantity, yet classical models (Almgren--Chriss, propagators) regress price on flow, which is biased whenever informed flow moves prices through information as well as trading. We present a proof-of-concept \emph{Causal Market Simulator}: a continuous-time causal prior-data fitted network (PFN) trained on a synthetic market prior in which a hidden informational flow confounds the flow--price relation by construction, with confounding strength an exact per-episode knob. On this prior, the naive estimator's bias follows a closed form we confirm empirically (up to 68\% overestimation), while the PFN tracks the unbiased true-parameter oracle at high confounding. Its \emph{do-ablated twin}, the same model with the intervention inputs removed, collapses onto the pre-window mean. Zero-shot, the model responds at the ground-truth scale to metaorders in an ABIDES limit-order book ($+0.38$ pre-onset standard deviations against seed-replay counterfactuals), and its intervention response replicates on about 2,300 detected flow bursts in BTC/ETH/SOL perpetuals and 3,800 on Nasdaq equities, evidence consistent with, though not proof of, causal transfer. Off-prior the response degrades gracefully, and split-conformal recalibration repairs interval calibration. Transfer hinges on encoding the metaorder as added flow rather than a clamped price level, not on more training. A recurrent state-space variant closes the remaining shape gap: its impact accrues over execution duration where the transformer's stays flat, raising the correlation with measured metaorder impact from $+0.68$ to between $+0.92$ and $+0.96$, at the cost of weaker on-prior deconfounding that traces to the training recipe rather than to recurrence.

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据路透社报道，Anthropic 的首次公开募股（IPO）招股书显示，公司首席执行官达里奥 · 阿莫迪（Dario Amodei） 去年总薪酬为 1,800 万美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1.21 亿元人民币） 。从薪酬规模来看，他处于主流科技企业高管梯队的中游水平。 阿莫迪的薪酬构成偏向于股票等多元化激励方式，与其他科技企业创始人类似，固定年薪仅占其个人财富总额的很小一部分。 据悉，达里奥 · 阿莫迪与其妹妹 ——Anthropic 总裁丹妮拉 · 阿莫迪（Daniela Amodei）的年薪在今年 7 月翻了一倍，均已达 140 万美元 （现汇率约合 940 万元人民币） 。 股票与股票期权奖励在二人 2025 年的薪酬方案中占据绝大部分，其中丹妮拉 · 阿莫迪去年的薪酬总额达 1,640 万美元 （现汇率约合 1.1 亿元人民币） 。 Anthropic 董事会今年以受限股票单位（RSU）的形式，承诺向兄妹二人追加股权激励。该部分权益约定在达成特定前置条件时方可正式兑现：部分权益与二人的在职期限挂钩，其余部分则与公司的 IPO 进程绑定。 首席财务官克里希纳 · 拉奥 (Krishna Rao) 去年的薪酬总额为 720,250 美元 （现汇率约合 483.6 万元人民币） 。拉奥于 2024 年入职时获授了 140 万股的期权配额，并在 2025 年行使了公允价值为 385,285 美元 （现汇率约合 258.7 万元人民币） 的期权。 Anthropic 发言人拒绝对上述财务数据置评。

_all_articles.title: 全球首次，爱立信、Verizon 宣布完成室外 6G 通话测试
_all_articles.title_original: 全球首次，爱立信、Verizon 宣布完成室外 6G 通话测试
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，美国电信运营商 Verizon 与爱立信宣布，双方在加利福尼亚州康科德市的一处 Verizon 商用网络站点，利用 7GHz 频段完成了 全球首次 6G 预标准技术现场通话测试 。 根据爱立信当地时间 15 日发布的新闻稿，爱立信的 6G 概念验证设备完成现场部署并通过验证，让 6G 技术 走出实验室 ，进入真实环境接受测试。双方不仅能够评估室外网络性能，还可以研究无线信号穿过建筑物进入室内后的表现。 IT之家注：“预标准 6G 技术”指 正式技术标准尚未确定、仍处于早期研发和测试阶段 的 6G 技术。 此次测试使用的爱立信 6G 概念验证设备，位于 Verizon 位于康科德市的商用网络站点。基站设在机房内，用户终端则放置在一座长约 3.7m、宽约 2.4m 的移动小屋中，可支持室内外两种固定无线测试配置。小屋配备独立电源和备用电池，并使用不同的墙体和窗户材料，以比较不同条件下的室内信号覆盖效果。测试采用尚未正式标准化的 6G 协议栈，载波带宽为 400MHz。 此次测试并非只针对无线信号穿透建筑物的能力。双方确认完成了 室外 6G 通话测试 ，同时还通过更全面的概念验证，研究 6G 信号从室外进入室内后的性能变化。测试内容包括网络覆盖、吞吐量、时延、稳定性和各项功能表现，并考虑了视距与非视距传播、植被和障碍物遮挡，以及信号穿过不同玻璃和建筑材料等实际情况。 双方强调，此次成果 仍属于 6G 正式标准出台前的概念验证 ，并不意味着 6G 开始商用。双方将继续分析现场测试数据，把获得的经验用于后续技术研究、测试及网络部署规划。 未来，6G 有望提供更 灵活的网络编程能力、更快的响应速度，以及感知使用环境的能力 ，为沉浸式通信、AI 原生服务、工业自动化和机器人应用创造更多可能。

_all_articles.title: SK 海力士拟在美新建 NAND 工厂，换取为中国工厂引进更多美国设备的机会
_all_articles.title_original: SK 海力士拟在美新建 NAND 工厂，换取为中国工厂引进更多美国设备的机会
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，路透社今日报道称，SK 海力士正试图以在美国建设新厂的方式，向美国政府换取为中国大连工厂引进更多美国制造的半导体设备的许可。 两名知情人士透露，SK 海力士希望通过提升中国工厂的产能，为美国新工厂提供资金支持，并逐步扩大其在美国的生产布局。 美国政府正推动 SK 海力士、三星电子等海外半导体企业赴美建厂，以提升美国本土制造能力并创造就业岗位。与此同时，人工智能和云计算数据中心需求增长，全球存储芯片供应趋紧，NAND 闪存价格持续上涨，也促使相关厂商考虑扩大生产。 据路透社报道，SK 海力士旗下美国子公司 Solidigm 希望在中国大连工厂尚未充分利用的厂房区域安装更多设备，用于生产 NAND 闪存。 据介绍，大连工厂使用的半导体设备来自美国厂商，包括泛林集团（Lam Research）、应用材料（Applied Materials）和科磊（KLA）。相关厂区名为 Mod B，于 2023 年建成，但由于当时存储市场低迷，设备安装工作未能完成。 知情人士称，该区域目前已经安装了部分设备，仍有空间容纳更多生产工具。Solidigm 已申请出口许可证，希望采购额外设备用于该区域。 SK 海力士向路透社表示，Mod B 的设备安装工作正在与美国政府密切协商、并在获得授权的情况下进行。该公司同时强调，目前并未寻求扩大大连 Mod B 的产能。Solidigm 则拒绝对此事置评。 路透社此前于 9 月报道称，Solidigm 正考虑在美国建设 NAND 闪存工厂，纽约州北部是当时的主要候选地点之一。知情人士表示，如果大连工厂能够提高产量，新增业务收入将有助于支付美国新工厂的建设费用，并为未来扩大美国本土生产提供过渡。另一名知情人士还透露，Solidigm 正考虑最早于 2027 年进行首次公开募股（IPO），以筹集可能用于新工厂建设的资金。 除美国新建 NAND 工厂的计划外，SK 海力士还在与英特尔洽谈租用其位于俄亥俄州、规划已久的半导体制造设施的部分空间。该公司也已在印第安纳州启动一座先进封装工厂的建设，主要面向高带宽内存（HBM）产品。

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，《华盛顿邮报》今日披露了一份白宫内部捐款记录，揭示了美国总统特朗普白宫宴会厅项目的主要捐赠方及具体金额。 记录显示，截至 9 月底共记录 67 笔超过 1 万美元 （现汇率约合 67,065 元人民币） 的捐款，私人捐赠承诺总额约为 3.33 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 22.33 亿元人民币） ，其中英伟达和苹果均承诺捐款 2,500 万美元 （现汇率约合 1.68 亿元人民币） ，均为单笔最高金额。 白宫此前于 2025 年 10 月公布过 37 名个人、企业及基金会的捐赠者名单，但未披露各自的捐款金额。这份内部电子表格记录了每笔捐款的来源、日期和金额。此次曝光的记录还显示，至少有 7,700 万美元 （现汇率约合 5.16 亿元人民币） 来自要求匿名的捐赠者。 值得注意的是，特朗普本人并未出现在此次捐款名单中 。白宫东翼旧建筑开始拆除数日后，特朗普曾表示，项目资金“100% 由我和一些朋友承担”。 根据《华盛顿邮报》此前的报道，特朗普曾表示希望为该项目筹集 4 亿美元 （现汇率约合 26.83 亿元人民币） ，而相关工程在 2026 年 3 月的成本估算已升至 6 亿美元 （现汇率约合 40.24 亿元人民币） ，其中包括宴会厅、办公空间及地下军事设施。相关记录显示，部分建设费用也使用了纳税人的资金。 英伟达是此次披露的主要捐赠方之一。文件显示，该公司于 2025 年 10 月承诺捐款 2,500 万美元 （现汇率约合 1.68 亿元人民币） ，并要求对捐赠来源保密。英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋此前曾公开表示，公司以“小规模”的方式支持白宫宴会厅项目，但未披露具体金额。英伟达发言人约翰・里佐回应称，公司支持美国的立场独立于其商业利益，并表示这笔捐款是向服务全体美国人的非党派信托机构作出的捐赠。 名单还披露了其他企业及个人的捐款情况。亚马逊、卡特彼勒、康卡斯特、微软和 T-Mobile 等企业均出现在主要捐赠方之列。加密货币企业及其投资者承诺捐款超过 1,800 万美元 （现汇率约合 1.21 亿元人民币） ，其中 Gemini 加密货币交易所联合创始人泰勒・温克莱沃斯和卡梅伦・温克莱沃斯兄弟合计捐赠了价值 505 万零 18 美元 （现汇率约合 120.7 元人民币） 的比特币。 部分捐赠者疑似还涉及利益交换。《华盛顿邮报》披露，Dish Network 联合创始人查尔斯・厄根承诺捐款总计 2,500 万美元 （现汇率约合 1.68 亿元人民币） ，分两次完成。此前，美国联邦通信委员会曾调查其旗下 EchoStar，并威胁撤销对该公司业务至关重要的政府许可证；在厄根与特朗普及联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹・卡尔会面后，相关调查于 2025 年 9 月结束。EchoStar 此后就出售部分频谱许可证达成交易，并于 2026 年 5 月获得联邦通信委员会及美国司法部批准。厄根及 EchoStar 拒绝就捐款问题置评。 此外，文件显示，Rocket 旗下子公司承诺捐款 1,000 万美元 （现汇率约合 6,706.5 万元人民币） ，时间为美国联邦住房金融局批准其收购 Mr. Cooper 三周后。Salesforce 首席执行官马克・贝尼奥夫及公司也分别承诺多笔捐款；其间，美国陆军于 2026 年 1 月向 Salesforce 授予一份最高价值 56 亿美元 （现汇率约合 375.56 亿元人民币） 、期限至 2035 年的合同。ServiceNow 则在美国总务管理局宣布与其达成联邦采购协议后，于 2025 年 10 月承诺捐款 500 万美元 （现汇率约合 3,353.2 万元人民币） 。相关企业均表示，捐款与政府审批或合同事项无关，政府部门也否认捐赠影响采购决策。 白宫发言人大卫・英格尔拒绝讨论具体捐款，但称捐赠者来自多家美国企业和个人，旨在改善白宫设施。 他还表示，政府将追查泄露文件的相关人员 。 当然，《华盛顿邮报》此次公布的名单并非完整名册，而是筹款团队内部用于追踪捐款的记录。报道指出，白宫此前公开列出的部分捐赠者，包括 Hard Rock International、Tether America 及模块化住宅企业高管 Paolo Tiramani，并未出现在这份记录中。相关方面尚未解释名单缺漏的原因。

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，台积电今日发布公告，截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日的第三季度： 合并收入 14,942.4 亿元新台币 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,109.51 亿元人民币） ， 同比增长 50.9%，环比增长 17.6% ； 净利润 7,630.6 亿元新台币 （现汇率约合 1,587.93 亿元人民币） ， 同比增长 68.7%，环比增长 8% ； 稀释每股收益 29.43 元新台币 （现汇率约合 6.1 元人民币） ， 同比增长 68.7% 。 以美元计，台积电第三季度收入为 467.2 亿美元 （现汇率约合 3,133.27 亿元人民币） ，同比增长 41.2%，环比增长 16.2%。 台积电第三季度毛利率为 66.4%，营业利润率为 58.7%， 净利润率为 51.1% 。 第三季度，台积电 2nm 出货占晶圆总收入的 8%；3nm 收入占 33%；5nm 收入占 28%；7nm 收入占 10%。先进技术（定义为 7nm 及更先进技术）占台积电晶圆总收入的 79%。

_all_articles.title: 尼康 Z5ⅡC 全画幅微单相机发售：主打新手入门，单机身 9999 元
_all_articles.title_original: 尼康 Z5ⅡC 全画幅微单相机发售：主打新手入门，单机身 9999 元
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，尼康 Z 5II C 全画幅微单相机于今日正式发售，黑色机身（不含镜头）售价为 9999 元。 该机定位新手入门，主打随手出片轻松拍，目前可叠加平台满 6000-780 元神券，券后 9219 元。 京东 尼康（Nikon）Z5IIC 全画幅微单相机 黑色机身 (不含镜头) 券后 9219 元 领 780 元券 Z5ⅡC 机身（黑色 / 银色）：RMB 9,999 元 Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-50mm f/4-6.3 套机：RMB 11,999 元 Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-105mm f/4-7.1 套机：RMB 12,799 元 Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-200mm f/4-6.3 VR 套机：RMB 15,499 元 其机身重 620 克，采用镁合金，提供银色和黑色两种配色，具备防尘防溅设计，使用轻巧便携、利于收纳的平顶设计和握持感稳固舒适的手柄。 Z5IIC 配备 24.5MP 全画幅背照式 CMOS 传感器与 EXPEED 7 图像处理器，支持 10 种类型的对象侦测，具有精准快速的自动对焦性能、最低达-10EV 的暗光对焦表现和最高约 1 秒的预拍功能。 尼康首次在全画幅无反中加入场景模式，共 15 种选项，覆盖人像、宠物、食物、夜景和黄昏等，还有自动调整拍摄参数的 AUTO 模式；支持五轴机身防抖，可提供最高 7.5 档补偿；还有胶片颗粒功能，可调整颗粒大小和强度。 用户选定场景后，相机自动优化色彩、亮度、白平衡和优化校准等设置。机身还设有专用按钮，可快速调用成像配方。 自动对焦基于深度学习，可检测并追踪人、狗、猫、鸟、车辆、飞机和鱼，支持眼部锁定。AUTO 模式会分析主体和场景，自动优化对焦、光圈、快门和 ISO。 这款新机还支持连接尼康云创和 SnapBridge，机身上专用的优化校准按钮可快速切换色彩方案，引入胶片颗粒功能，轻松打造个性化的影像风格。 该机采用 3.2 英寸可变角度监视器，可翻转用于自拍和 Vlog；连拍速度最高约 14fps，高速帧捕获 + 模式下可达 30fps，并支持预拍摄，记录快门释放前最多 1 秒；视频支持 4K UHD 60fps、Full HD 120fps，以及 4 倍和 5 倍慢动作。 视频方面，该机还支持 H.265 10-bit MOV、N-Log 和 N-RAW 录制至 SD 卡。通过 USB 连接 PC，可使用 UVC / UAC 进行直播。尼康称，Z5IIC 的“C”代表 casual，即休闲，旨在通过直观控制和自动化功能降低全画幅使用门槛。 IT之家附详细参数如下： 京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次： 点此抽红包 。 淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次： 点此抽红包 。

_all_articles.title: 昆仑万维发布世界首款消费级显卡视频大模型游戏，同步开源
_all_articles.title_original: 昆仑万维发布世界首款消费级显卡视频大模型游戏，同步开源
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，昆仑万维今日发布世界上第一款运行在单张消费级显卡上的视频大模型游戏 ——Matrix-Game 4.0。 昆仑万维介绍称，“Matrix-Game 4.0 构建起了游戏世界模型的新范式：由游戏引擎维护世界状态与交互规则，由视频生成模型实时呈现精细画面。它把 480p、60 FPS 的实时游戏体验，装进了一张 NVIDIA RTX 5090；从你按下按键，到画面做出反应，延迟低于 150 毫秒。Matrix-Game 4.0 首次跑通了‘代码生成游戏逻辑 → 结构画面提供结构约束 → 视频模型实时渲染’的完整闭环，让游戏原型开发、个性化定制与 UGC 从此拥有了真正可落地的技术路径。项目已同步开源。” IT之家注意到，Matrix-Game 4.0 在发布时同步开源，未来，团队将持续迭代模型：部署 refiner 提高画面分辨率，探索跨玩家视角保持一致的多人联机体验，提供更细粒度的画面控制，并拓展对更多游戏类型与场景的支持。 开源地址及项目网站： Github： https://github.com/SkyworkAI/Matrix-Game.git Huggingface： https://huggingface.co/Skywork/Matrix-Game-4.0 项目网站： https://matrix-game-v4-0.github.io/page/

_all_articles.title: 中国科学家首次用中国大模型攻克世界级数学难题，曾困扰学界 30 余年
_all_articles.title_original: 中国科学家首次用中国大模型攻克世界级数学难题，曾困扰学界 30 余年
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，上海人工智能实验室今日发文，困扰数学界 30 余年的世界级难题 —— 三维 Ghys 猜想 迎来了破解。 上海人工智能实验室访问学者、大湾区大学教授许地生团队依托书生科学多模态大模型 S2（书生-S2），基于“通专融合”技术路径， 通过人机协同完成了三维 Ghys 猜想证明 。 北京大学董彬教授、刘若川院士团队利用其开发的 SHEAF 框架对本次证明完成形式化验证，验证了这一工作的正确性。 这标志着中国科学家首次用中国大模型攻克世界级数学难题 。 Ghys 猜想由法国数学家艾蒂安 · 吉斯（Étienne Ghys）于 1995 年提出，猜测每一个紧致复流形上的全纯 Anosov 系统，都双全纯共轭于某个复 infra-幂零流形上的全纯仿射自同构。该问题兼具理论难度与学科标志性价值，被动力系统领域数学专家公认为该领域重要的长期公开问题之一，是检验数学推理能力的一块试金石。 相关论文已在预印本平台（arXiv）发布，其形式化代码也在 Github 平台公开。IT之家附链接如下： https://github.com/frenzymath/HolomorphicAnosov 上海人工智能实验室表示，本项研究的意义还在于验证了一种新的科研范式。传统数学研究依赖个体天才的漫长摸索，而本次攻关将专家直觉系统性接入机器求解回路，形成“系统探索 — 专家判断 — 成果积累 — 反馈修正”的闭环。 这一范式可复制推广至更多“搜索空间巨大而专家稀缺”的基础研究领域，实现更多“从 0 到 1”的原始创新突破 。 接下来，依托本次研究跑通的完整能力闭环，团队将进一步封装为书生 · 端砚科学发现平台可复用的数学验证模块，供后续科学问题研究直接调用。同时，以三维 Ghys 猜想的突破作为起点， 上海人工智能实验室将沉淀的推理能力扩展应用于数学结构同源的其他学科 ；取得新突破后，再将新推理能力封装回端砚平台复用，与更多学科结合寻求下一轮突破，形成“突破 — 封装 — 复用 — 再突破”的自进化飞轮。

_all_articles.title_original: 游改真人电影《生化危机：爆发夜》上映 10 天，票房累计破 3.04 亿
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，电影《生化危机：爆发夜》官方微博今日宣布， 本片上映第 10 天，票房累计破 3.04 亿 。 IT之家附该电影官方简介如下： 嘘，别出声。 黑暗中的生化怪物正在凝视，楼顶上的嗜血异种们虎视眈眈。 城市变为血色废墟，危险即将全面爆发！检查好手中的武器，抱紧需要运送的快递。前方高能，浣熊市的求生副本即将开启，请做好逃离准备。 这部惊悚片此前已经在海外上映，在烂番茄上首映获得 96% 的新鲜度，成为有史以来评分最高的电子游戏改编电影作品。全球首周票房 1.08 亿美元 （现汇率约合 7.24 亿元人民币） ，创该系列最高开画纪录。 本片根据热门恐怖游戏《生化危机》改编，这也是该 IP 的最新一部院线电影，由《凶器》《野蛮人》导演扎克・克雷格倾力打造，奥斯汀 · 艾布拉姆斯、保罗 · 沃尔特 · 豪泽、扎克 · 切利、卡莉 · 瑞斯参与主演。 本片将讲述奉命奔赴浣熊市的医疗速递员布莱恩，却意外深陷全城失控的病毒浩劫的故事。电影官方提醒：未成年人谨慎观看。 值得一提的是，导演扎克 · 克雷格此前回应了为何弃用里昂， 他并不想重讲里昂的故事，也不打算复刻原版游戏剧情 。克雷格强调，全新《生化危机》电影并不是某款游戏或角色剧情的改编，而是发生在《生化危机》世界观的全新故事，时间线大致与《生化危机 2》相同。 IT之家小伙伴记得用 最会买购买电影票 ，享受折扣价的同时还可以获得返利，预计每张票可以节省 5~15 元！

_all_articles.title: PS5 越狱商店 Overdrive 被索尼勒令关停后，克隆版本数小时内重新上线
_all_articles.title_original: PS5 越狱商店 Overdrive 被索尼勒令关停后，克隆版本数小时内重新上线
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，索尼 SIE 已开始对 PS5 越狱开发者采取法律行动，一个名为 Overdrive 的游戏商店已被关闭。不过，原项目关闭后，GitHub 上随即又出现了两个新的仓库，分别为原项目的分支版本和使用不同账号发布的克隆版本。 X 用户 Oliver Darko 反馈称，索尼互动娱乐的律师已向 Overdrive 开发者发送停止侵权函，该商店目前已下架，其 GitHub 页面显示 404 错误。 IT之家注：Overdrive 是一个面向已越狱 PS5 主机的非官方游戏商店，于 10 月 9 日在 GitHub 上发布，提供超过 1600 款 PS4 和 PS5 游戏的免费下载，界面类似于 PlayStation Store，但所有游戏均为免费，库中包含《黑神话：悟空》《漫威蜘蛛侠 2》和《赛博朋克 2077》等作品。 据 Notebookcheck 报道，自制软件内容创作者 Edigax 于 10 月 11 日在 X 上发布了一段 Overdrive 的实际运行视频，该视频随后被 RinoTheBouncer 等账号转发，播放量达到约 700 万次。配合 ShadowMountPlus 等工具使用时，Overdrive 下载的游戏可直接出现在 PS5 主屏幕上。 Overdrive 的走红与 PS5 越狱社区近期的活跃直接相关。9 月底，一个名为 Relapse 的公开越狱工具发布，支持固件版本 7.00 至 13.60 的 PS5 和 PS5 Pro 主机，大幅扩展了可越狱设备的范围。 此后，PS5 越狱社区涌现出大量自制应用，包括模拟器、启动器和串流工具，甚至还有人在 PS5 上实现了原生运行 Xbox 云游戏的壮举。 索尼对此的回应是先后推送了 14.00 和 14.10 固件更新，封堵了已知漏洞。Relapse 目前不支持 14.00 及以上固件，且没有官方降级路径，用户一旦更新系统便会失去越狱能力。 据 VideoCardz 报道，Overdrive 被关闭后不久，GitHub 上便出现了两个新的项目仓库。其中一个是对原始项目的 fork，另一个则是在不同账号下发布的克隆版本。原仓库位于 half144 账号下，现已无法访问，但新的发布页面提供了最新版本下载以及现有用户的迁移指引。 有分析认为，即便索尼能够持续下架主仓库，已经分发的代码副本和社区 fork 使得该项目难以被彻底清除。 社区对 Overdrive 的态度呈现出明显的对抗色彩。据 Notebookcheck 报道，不少评论者将 Overdrive 视为对索尼逐步取消实体游戏的回击，有用户评论称“全数字游戏，正如索尼所愿”。 相关阅读： 《 PS5 游戏机黑商店“Overdrive”停止运营，索尼疑似发函 》 《 玩家为破解后的索尼 PS5 游戏机开发自制应用商店，可免费下载各大作品 》

_all_articles.title: 光刻机巨头 ASML 阿斯麦第三季度营收 116.6 亿欧元创新高：净利润 50 亿欧元，需求排到 2030 年
_all_articles.title_original: 光刻机巨头 ASML 阿斯麦第三季度营收 116.6 亿欧元创新高：净利润 50 亿欧元，需求排到 2030 年
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，光刻机巨头 ASML 阿斯麦今日发布公告，2026 年第三季度实现创纪录的 116.6 亿欧元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 874.01 亿元人民币） 净销售额，毛利率为 57.5%， 净利润为 50 亿欧元 （现汇率约合 374.79 亿元人民币） 。 ASML 预计 2026 年第四季度净销售额在 142 亿至 152 亿欧元 （现汇率约合 1,064.4 亿至 1,139.36 亿元人民币） 之间，毛利率约为 57%。 ASML 预计 2026 年全年净销售额预计在 440 亿至 450 亿欧元 （现汇率约合 3,298.16 亿至 3,373.11 亿元人民币） 之间，毛利率约为 56%。 ASML 总裁兼 CEO Christophe Fouquet 表示， 一些客户表达了对 2029 年甚至 2030 年订单的兴趣 。“鉴于如此强劲订单量持续增长需求，我们现在预计 2027 年和 2028 年的供应计划将无法完全满足客户需求。鉴于此，我们正在研究将 2028 年产能提升到超过之前公布的 30% 增长的方案。此外，我们通过生产力升级产品组合，持续为客户提供大量晶圆产能。”

_all_articles.title: 为支付离婚补偿金，SK 集团会长崔泰源向戴尔创始人基金出售 5440 亿韩元 SK Inc 股权
_all_articles.title_original: 为支付离婚补偿金，SK 集团会长崔泰源向戴尔创始人基金出售 5440 亿韩元 SK Inc 股权
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间周三披露的监管申报文件显示，SK 集团会长崔泰源已达成交易，将控股公司 SK Inc 1.34% 的股份出售给与戴尔科技（Dell Technologies）创始人迈克尔 · 戴尔相关联的投资基金，交易金额为 5,440 亿韩元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 27.31 亿元人民币） 。 本次交易是崔泰源股份减持筹资计划的一部分，他计划通过出售股票总共筹集 9,440 亿韩元 （现汇率约合 47.4 亿元人民币） ，用于向前妻支付离婚补偿金。 申报文件以及 DFO 管理公司官网信息显示，本次 972493 股 SK Inc 股份的买方为 DFO Public Investments, L.P .。这是一家注册于特拉华州的投资基金，隶属于迈克尔 · 戴尔家族投资办公室 DFO Management。 本月早些时候，SK Inc 在申报材料中披露，崔泰源同意出售 165 万股股份（占比 2.26%），总对价 9,440 亿韩元 （现汇率约合 47.4 亿元人民币） 。其中 681431 股（0.94% 股权），将以 4,000 亿韩元 （现汇率约合 20.08 亿元人民币） 出售给韩国投资证券。 对于剩余股份的买家，SK 此前仅称其为战略投资者，表示该投资者在考量 SK Inc 的企业竞争力与中长期增长前景后，同意收购这笔股权。 戴尔科技是 AI 服务器与数据中心基础设施的核心供应商，与 SK 集团旗下存储芯片子公司 SK 海力士存在业务往来。值得注意的是，收购股权的是戴尔家族投资基金，并非戴尔科技公司本身。 路透社 5 月曾报道，在 AI 需求爆发背景下，多家全球科技企业接洽 SK 海力士，提出投资专用存储芯片产线，协助承担高昂生产设备投入，以此保障芯片供货。 韩国公司治理论坛表示，如果崔泰源和买方达成约定（哪怕只是口头约定）、保持投票权行动一致，二者就必须将所持股份合并披露为共同持股。该机构称，不履行该披露义务将违反韩国资本市场法。 该论坛是独立监督机构，负责监察韩国企业治理相关事务。论坛提出，这名战略投资者与崔泰源存在利益协同的可能性，该基金存在被法律认定为与崔泰源构成共同持股方的风险。

_all_articles.title: 自动驾驶公司 Applied Intuition 获得投资邀约，估值达 300 亿美元
_all_articles.title_original: 自动驾驶公司 Applied Intuition 获得投资邀约，估值达 300 亿美元
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，据 The Information 今天报道，自动驾驶初创公司 Applied Intuition 已收到多份投资邀约， 估值最少 300 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,011.75 亿元人民币） ，相比 6 月估值翻了一番。 据报道，Applied Intuition 由前 Y Combinator 首席运营官 Qasar Younis 和前谷歌产品经理 Peter Ludwig 联合创立，该公司专注于自动驾驶软件而非车辆制造。2024 年底，该公司年度经常性收入达 4 亿美元 （现汇率约合 26.82 亿元人民币） 。 Applied Intuition 此前从 Andreessen Horowitz 和 General Catalyst 等机构筹集 12 亿美元 （现汇率约合 80.47 亿元人民币） 资金，其主要客户有五十铃、大众等。

_all_articles.title: “中国刻蚀机之父”尹志尧：AI 有可能会出现泡沫，这点大家需要多加留意
_all_articles.title_original: “中国刻蚀机之父”尹志尧：AI 有可能会出现泡沫，这点大家需要多加留意
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，第 26 届中国国际工业博览会昨日于上海开幕。在当日下午举行的集成电路高峰论坛上，中微公司董事长兼总经理尹志尧在分析行业趋势时，谈及了 AI 话题。 ▲ 图源：中微公司官微 | 中微公司董事长兼总经理尹志尧博士发表演讲 他表示，现在 AI 话题非常火热，几乎所有会议都在谈 AI，但自己要提出一个警示： AI 有可能会出现泡沫，这点大家需要多加留意 。 尹志尧称，回看 1984—2026 年全球半导体行业 CAPEX 的年度增减曲线，波动十分剧烈，行业资本开支一年增幅可以达到 100%，也可以一年下滑 30%，还会出现连续下行。 未来我们仍可能经历行业周期性变化，要思考的是如何去应对这种周期波动 。 今年 8 月，在美国企业持续向 AI 数据中心扩张计划投入巨额投机性资本之际，欧洲监管机构已经开始考虑即将到来的 AI 泡沫破裂。欧洲主要银行机构表示， 市场很可能出现调整，而且这种冲击不会放过世界任何一个地区或任何一个人 。 IT之家注：尹志尧被称为“中国刻蚀机之父”，是首位入职英特尔的中国留学生，在美国工作 20 多年，手握几百项专利，一手托起两家世界顶尖设备公司。 60 岁时，尹志尧毅然放弃百万年薪回国创业，彼时中国半导体设备市场几乎一片空白，随后他创立并带领中微公司成为与曾经工作过的美国公司齐名的刻蚀机巨头之一。

_all_articles.title: 微软逆转办公 AI 策略，新版 Copilot 整合完整 Word / Excel / PowerPoint 体验
_all_articles.title_original: 微软逆转办公 AI 策略，新版 Copilot 整合完整 Word / Excel / PowerPoint 体验
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 昨日（10 月 12 日）发布博文，报道称微软逆转办公 AI 策略，此前主要将 Copilot 嵌入到 Office 应用中， 而现在围绕着新款 Copilot 应用，集成完整的 Word、Excel 和 PowerPoint 创建、编辑与协作体验。 IT之家附上相关视频如下： 根据微软演示，用户在 Copilot 应用中，无需切换至独立 Office 应用，即可创建、编辑 Word 文档、Excel 表格和 PowerPoint 演示文稿，并与其他用户协作。 在全新 Copilot 应用中 ，用户可从 Copilot Chat 中的简单提示启动任务，也可通过 Copilot Cowork 发起更复杂的任务。例如，用户可要求 Copilot 依据研究笔记生成 Word 文档，系统随后在对话旁打开该文档。 与旧版 Copilot 仅能创建 Office 文件不同，新版支持用户在 Copilot 内继续处理文件。用户可要求 AI 重写内容、添加表格或完成其他修改，也可使用标准 Office 编辑控件手动调整内容。 协作方面，用户可在应用内共享文件、添加评论，并与他人共同编辑；其他用户的更改会实时显示。目前支持编辑的文件类型包括 Word、Excel 和 PowerPoint。 微软同时在 Copilot 应用中推出“库”（Library）版块，集中呈现最近使用的 Office 文件、Copilot 页面和 AI 生成图像。用户可从该版块重新打开既有文件或创建新文件。 所有 Office 文件仍存储于 OneDrive，并保留格式、注释、共享权限和版本历史。模型调用方面，用户可为 Office 任务选择指定 AI 模型，也可启用 Auto 模式，由 Copilot 依据任务自动选择模型。

_all_articles.title: 小米门窗传感器 3 开启众筹：3 年长续航、开合及时感知，44 元
_all_articles.title_original: 小米门窗传感器 3 开启众筹：3 年长续航、开合及时感知，44 元
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，小米门窗传感器 3 今日在小米有品开启众筹，活动截止时间为 10 月 19 日 10 点，众筹价 44 元（ 点击前往 ）。 IT之家注意到，新品主打“一次安装、3 年省心长续航”，围绕门窗、抽屉、柜门等开合状态感知，进一步强化家庭安防与智能联动体验。 与前代相比，小米门窗传感器 3 将传感方案升级为隧道磁阻传感器，官方称其较传统霍尔传感器响应更快、功耗更低； 续航标称可达 3 年 ，采用 CR2032 纽扣电池与低功耗设计，电量不足时可通过米家 App 推送低电提醒。 功能上，新品支持开合状态查看、感应记录、当日开合次数统计以及开启 / 关闭时长统计；作为对比，上代门窗传感器 2 采用霍尔传感器、提供 1 年续航并配备光照传感器，而三代更强调长续航与开合行为记录。 实际使用中，用户需搭配具备 蓝牙 Mesh 网关 功能的设备，方可在米家 App 远程查看门窗、抽屉、储物柜等开闭状态与感应记录；异常状态时，App 可推送远程通知。借助小米澎湃智联，传感器可与智能开关、空调伴侣、水浸卫士、温湿度计等设备组成场景：例如开门自动亮灯、开窗联动关闭空调、雨天或湿度过高时提醒关窗等。官方也提示，相关自动化需提前在米家 App 设置，联动设备需单独购买，部分能力以实际使用为准。 设计方面，新品机身小巧轻薄，适用于门窗、抽屉、柜门、收纳箱等窄边空间；机身印有安装方向指引，主体与磁铁对应关系更清晰，以降低反装导致感应失效的概率。

_all_articles.title: 2K＋185Hz，维信诺 × iQOO × 清华大学屏幕技术沟通会定档 10 月 14 日
_all_articles.title_original: 2K＋185Hz，维信诺 × iQOO × 清华大学屏幕技术沟通会定档 10 月 14 日
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，iQOO 手机今日宣布，维信诺 ×iQOO× 清华大学屏幕技术沟通会，10 月 14 日 19:00 见。据介绍，iQOO Neo12 手机将搭载 2K＋185Hz 显示屏，官方宣称“难度远不止参数相加”。 在此之前，iQOO Neo12 手机已官宣首发搭载 pTSF 技术的 2K 185Hz 超冠屏，超高清与超高刷并发，通透与省电兼得，本月见。 此外，该机还搭载第五代骁龙 8 至尊版处理器 + 冰穹风冷散热系统，配备自研电竞芯片 Q3，支持光追、超分、超帧、滤镜、游戏相机。新机内置 9000mAh 蓝海大电池，采用单电芯设计、第五代硅负极技术，能量密度高达 916Wh/L。 关于 iQOO Neo12 手机的更多消息，感兴趣的朋友可以关注IT之家后续报道。

_all_articles.title_original: LG Display：FLiPP OLED 具备原料利用率与生产效率优势，将率先用于 IT 产品
_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，LG Display 当地时间本月 8 日举行了 FLiPP 技术研讨会，企业首席技术官최영석 介绍了这一 FMM-less OLED 方案的技术优势。 LG Display 表示，FLiPP OLED 在第八代玻璃基板上生产时无需半切， 可直接全幅制造 ，这带来了原料利用率上的优势。 如果都生产 23.5" 面板，半切 FMM 工艺的边角利用率仅有 75%，而免半切 FLiPP 则能 将边角利用率提升到 93% 以上 。半切 FMM 的有机 EL 材料沉积效率仅有 40%， FLiPP 则能达到 74% 。 此外，FLiPP OLED 可利用现有的 WOLED 生产基础设施，支持流水线式沉积作业，减少了重复工序以及工序间隔，每个基板的沉积时间也更短， 整体沉积工艺用时缩短了 40% 。 LG Display 计划首先在平板电脑和笔记本电脑这两类 IT 显示面板上应用 FLiPP 工艺，并逐步扩展到可穿戴设备、电视领域。这项技术 还支持 XR 领域应用 。 相关阅读： 《 消息称 LG Display 计划在坡州 E4 产线进行 FLiPP OLED 量产验证 》 《 LG Display 首度展示 FMM-less OLED 像素沉积图案化技术 FLiPP 》

_all_articles.summary: IT之家 10 月 10 日消息，今日，据彭博社援引知情人士消息，半导体公司 Cirrus Logic Inc. 上个月向 Synaptics Inc. 提出了一项未经请求的收购要约，试图破坏后者此前已公布的、与安森美半导体的并购交易。 知情人士表示，Synaptics 周四更新的股东委托文件中提及的“甲方”， 正是 Cirrus Logic 。知情人士补充，目前尚不清楚 Cirrus Logic 是否仍有意推进这笔收购。 据悉，Cirrus Logic 的报价采用现金 + 股票形式，促使安森美在上周修改了与 Synaptics 的协议条款。安森美将交易结构从全股票改为全现金，每股报价调整至 123 美元。安森美在一份声明中称，此次调整源于第三方提出的“竞争性非邀约收购提案”，但当时并未披露竞购方身份。 IT之家注意到，安森美于今年 6 月宣布，将以全股票对价收购边缘 AI 芯片企业 Synaptics，这笔交易价值约 70 亿美元 （现汇率约合 469.45 亿元人民币） ， 预计 2027 年中完成 。 然而，双方于本月初修订协议，安森美将以约 57 亿美元 （现汇率约合 382.27 亿元人民币） 的现金完成该笔交易，而不是此前公布的 70 亿美元 （现汇率约合 469.45 亿元人民币） 股票，这对应 18.6% 的折让。安森美表示此次修订是由于收到 第三方主动提出的竞争性收购方案 ，预计此次交易将立即提升其 Non-GAAP 每股收益，并为 Synaptics 的股东带来价值确定性。 相关阅读： 《 自身股价下跌，安森美将收购 Synaptics 的对价调整为 57 亿美元现金 》 《 安森美将换股收购边缘 AI 芯片企业 Synaptics，交易价值 70 亿美元 》

_all_articles.title: Contextual Credit Policy Optimization
_all_articles.title_original: Contextual Credit Policy Optimization
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.19103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning enables large language model agents to learn from sparse outcome rewards in long-horizon tasks. Recent methods derive step-level credit by comparing observation-matched experiences across trajectories. However, identical observations can occur in different contexts, and matched peers are not equally informative for a given decision. Moreover, favorable terminal outcomes can obscure redundant actions or detours within successful trajectories. To address these two challenges, we propose Contextual Credit Policy Optimization (CCPO). For the first, CCPO weights observation-matched peers from other trajectories by contextual similarity, computed from frozen LLM representations and accumulated trajectory statistics, allowing peers from similar contexts to contribute more to a step's baseline. For the second, CCPO pairs historical credit, which compares the realized return against the weighted peer baseline, with future credit, which measures the change in contextual outcome value over a short realized continuation. A step is thus credited for the progress it makes, not only for its trajectory's eventual outcome. Both credits are computed in hindsight from rollouts already collected for training, enabling CCPO to address these challenges without an auxiliary value critic. Across two Qwen2.5-Instruct backbones (1.5B and 7B), CCPO achieves up to 97.4% success on ALFWorld and 79.4% on WebShop and outperforms GRPO by up to 21.6 and 18.5 points. Ablations show that contextual weighting outperforms uniform weighting, and that historical and future credit serve as complementary learning signals.

_all_articles.title: Beyond Binary Verifiable Rewards: Behavioral Self-Rewarding for SWE Agents
_all_articles.title_original: Beyond Binary Verifiable Rewards: Behavioral Self-Rewarding for SWE Agents
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision for software engineering agents through executable tests, but binary rewards fail to distinguish trajectories with substantially different debugging quality. We investigate whether the current policy can judge its own trajectories and use these judgments to improve task performance without a separately trained reward model. To this end, we introduce Behavioral Self-Rewarding (BSR), a reward-refinement method that reuses the policy to compare observable debugging behavior among trajectories from the same task with the same verifier outcome. BSR aggregates pairwise preferences into task-local scores and converts them into bounded auxiliary rewards, introducing reward contrast while preserving the verifier-defined pass/fail ordering. This provides additional supervision from already-collected trajectories without requiring new environment interactions. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench-Live show consistent improvements across the evaluated Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B configurations, supporting using the policy's own comparative judgments as a complementary learning signal for training software engineering agents.

_all_articles.title: What blog posts influenced your thinking the most?
_all_articles.title_original: What blog posts influenced your thinking the most?
_all_articles.summary: My comment on What blog posts influenced your thinking the most? — Lobste.rs. An early Joel Spolsky one for me was The Law of Leaky Abstractions . I read that near the start of my career and it's encouraged me to always be looking for improved understanding of the layers under where I'm working, just in case one of those abstractions leaks. A more recent one, from 2018, is Migrations: the sole scalable fix to tech debt by Will Larson. I absolutely love his idea that migrations (e.g. replacing one service with a new one, or switching database engines, or whatever) are part and parcel of software engineering and are a skill that you should invest in and get good at, not avoid or treat as special one-offs. The Engineer/Manager Pendulum by Charity Majors was hugely influential for me. I was stuck in engineering management and worried that if I switched back to being an "Individual Contributor" (ugh I hate that term) I'd damage my career. Charity gave me permission to make the switch by pointing out that many of the most successful software developers pendulum from one track to the other multiple times over their career, and doing so makes you better at both sides. Tags: joel-spolsky , software-engineering , will-larson , charity-majors

_all_articles.title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
_all_articles.title_original: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. PolarGD reaches the minimizer in one step whenever the rows of the error are orthogonal with equal norms, for any Hessian, whereas gradient descent needs all Hessian eigenvalues to be equal; and unlike sign descent, PolarGD is unaffected by rotations of the problem. Over many steps, PolarGD acts as gradient descent preconditioned by the current iterate, so its speed is governed by the conditioning of the iterate rather than of the Hessian. This explains fast regimes as well as a slow one, caused by tiny singular values of the iterate, in which PolarGD is much slower than gradient descent. Finally, the few Newton-Schulz iterations used in Muon treat these tiny singular values as gradient descent does, so fewer iterations can converge faster than exact orthogonalization; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of the singular values of the attention matrices fall in this regime.

_all_articles.title: Climbing the Ladder: Automating Data Pipelines and Reproducing Baselines in Low-Resource Settings
_all_articles.title_original: Climbing the Ladder: Automating Data Pipelines and Reproducing Baselines in Low-Resource Settings
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The massively multilingual translation systems that now include Sicilian learned it from noisy, non-standardised web text. To obtain better translation quality, we redevelop the small neural machine translation (NMT) system that Wdowiak customized for Sicilian. We rebuild on maintained software the extraction of the parallel text from the PDFs of the bilingual journal Arba Sicula, whose sentences are aligned by a language-agnostic sentence encoder with thresholds tuned against an existing hand alignment and then filtered for the typical errors of automatic alignment. Furthermore, the tokenization and the desinence-biased subword segmentation of the original system are ported to a Perl-free implementation, and all the results are measured on a frozen test set drawn from the journal. We compare small Transformers trained from scratch with the pretrained NLLB model adapted by low-rank fine-tuning, in both directions and with Italian as a closely related bridge language, and we adapt to the pretrained model the reverse-training recipe of the original system, i.e., a stage on forward-scored back-translations of the web Sicilian followed by a stage on the curated literary text. The pretrained model is by far the better of the two, and the staged training improves the translation into Sicilian more than the translation from it. On the test set of the original system, and in the tokenized space in which it was scored, the staged model with a larger adapter and more back-translations is above the reverse-training recipe in the directions that involve English and below it between Sicilian and Italian. Yet, a multilingual adapter degrades the directions on which it was not trained, which limits its use as a general multilingual model.

_all_articles.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
_all_articles.title_original: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech synthesized via a multi-speaker, dual-engine TTS pipeline; Stage 2 explores Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with transcription and script rewards. We find that synthetic SFT provides the primary cross-domain transfer to spontaneous human speech, reducing Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40% to 21.52% (-1.88 pp) and switch-point error rate (SPER) from 35.89% to 28.77% (-7.12 pp). Subsequent GRPO yields small, statistically significant adjustments on 173 test utterances (1.69%), driving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45% to 6.36% (p <= 0.001) and SPER to 28.70% (p = 0.022 clustered). Crucially, ablation reveals that in this SFT-converged encoder-decoder setting, an auxiliary script reward term yields performance identical to MER-only optimization because rollout candidate groups exhibit near-zero script variance on synthetic data. On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp (stabilizing at 18.42% after GRPO, a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while preserving English lexical WER (3.38% vs. 3.33%). Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.

_all_articles.title: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing
_all_articles.title_original: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) models can estimate item parameters through an item response decoder trained solely for next-response prediction, yet predictive accuracy does not guarantee parameter recovery. We study 2PL, GPCM, and NRM decoders paired with LSTM, Transformer, and DKVMN encoders. Response-model derivatives show why discrimination and option slope updates depend directly on the scale and spread of estimated ability. Affine logit identities show how item-dependent shifts and rescaling in estimated ability are absorbed into item parameters without changing response probabilities. In simulations, difficulty, mean threshold, and correct-option intercept recovery remain high under shuffled order across representation widths, whereas discrimination and keyed option slope contrast recovery require wider item representations and degrade further under fixed item order. Separating the sequence item representation (width $d_S$) from the item parameter key (width $d_M$), and pairing a wide key with a thin sequence representation ($\mathrm{SK}(64,8)$), reduces fixed-order ability distortions and improves recovery and cross-order consistency without sacrificing test accuracy or increasing model size relative to a shared width-64 baseline ($\mathrm{SH}(64)$). On TIMSS and EdNet, widening $d_M$ consistently improves agreement with an offline IRT reference, while the trade-off from narrowing $d_S$ depends on the encoder's reliance on sequence width for prediction. These findings show why item parameters, especially discrimination and option slopes, must be evaluated separately from response prediction.

_all_articles.title: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations
_all_articles.title_original: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learned representations of high-dimensional multimodal health records are increasingly used to adjust for confounding, yet they are usually trained to reconstruct the data rather than preserve the information that causal identification requires. We study counterfactual outcomes under alternative treatments, including phenotype-specific effects and patient-level counterfactual risk profiles of the kind digital twins provide, and interventional direct and indirect effects under exposure-induced intermediate confounding. We give conditions under which a representation preserves identification and show that interventional mediation is more demanding than counterfactual comparison. We prove that no covariate-only training objective, whether reconstruction, contrastive, or physics-informed, can certify that a representation is sufficient, and that, in a linear structural model, a representation can lose arbitrarily little reconstruction accuracy yet induce arbitrarily large bias. We decompose the error of cross-fitted doubly robust estimators into a first-order representation bias, which neither double robustness nor cross-fitting removes, and a second-order remainder of nuisance-estimation errors, so coverage worsens as the sample size grows when the representation is insufficient. We propose a workflow combining modality-specific variational autoencoders trained outside the estimation sample, cross-fitted doubly robust estimators, locked phenotypes, select-then-confirm pathway analysis, portable representations, and diagnostics for representation insufficiency, exposure leakage, and sensitivity. In simulations, discarding a rare, moderately strong confounder gave indirect-effect intervals with 2% coverage at n = 3,000; reconstruction loss missed the problem, and a simple predictive diagnostic flagged it in every replicate.

_all_articles.title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
_all_articles.title_original: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.

_all_articles.title: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades
_all_articles.title_original: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper charts the evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical -- Intelligent Reasoning by Example from print with runnable programmes on a 3.5-inch diskette published in 1994, via various intermediate online versions, to the fully interactive online edition available today. Our aim is to investigate -- from both the writer's and the reader's perspectives -- the potential impact of technology on educational materials. The three authors of this paper present three distinct and complementary points of view, which come together to shape an interactive online book that offers an immersive learning experience. Peter describes the philosophy behind the original book and experiences teaching from it. Jan demonstrates how contemporary web programming has enabled a fully interactive realisation of the book's philosophy. Kacper reports how different technologies can be adopted to build a versatile authoring toolkit that underpins the interactive online edition of the book. Collating these distinct yet coherent perspectives allows us to reflect on future opportunities for interactive Prolog teaching materials arising from the continuous development of web technologies. The insights we offer should be of interest to teachers of Prolog as well as those wanting to find out about the latest educational technologies.

_all_articles.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
_all_articles.title_original: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilingual large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where visible reasoning traces support verification, education, and safety auditing, yet standard evaluations typically measure only final-answer agreement or holistic response similarity. As a result, they establish outcome consistency without determining whether users across languages receive comparable supporting evidence. We introduce a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity, with pair-specific calibration to enable comparison across languages. Across three reasoning benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, the natural baseline---embedding each whole response and comparing the two by cosine---systematically overstates agreement: $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ of examples in the top quartile of holistic similarity are not in the top quartile of structural similarity. This dissociation is stable across sentence encoders and step segmentations, and blind bilingual annotation studies in two English-anchored language pairs show that human judgments align with structural similarity rather than with the holistic baseline. A same-language control shows that the level of divergence is language-specific: two English traces for paraphrases of the same question agree more closely than an English trace and its counterparts in other languages. Our results show that answer-level and holistic evaluations can substantially overestimate the consistency of multilingual explanatory artifacts, motivating trace-level evaluation for reliable multilingual deployment.

_all_articles.title: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
_all_articles.title_original: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.30664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. We show that this serialization is unnecessary for bounded-horizon control: the reachable future forms a shallow action-prefix tree, which we compile --- one root prefill plus one tree-causal probe evaluate every prefix-conditioned action distribution with serial decoding's tokens, positions, and causal ancestry. A prefix-state lemma makes compiled control policy-exact in exact arithmetic: the same policy with a two-forward critical path and zero output tokens. One further probe pass certifies the exact order-marginalized MAP set. Across four document-disjoint splits and two scales on the primary MetaX device, compiled control matches the serial policy on $84$--$89\%$ of questions --- every instrumented divergence a floating-point near-tie --- and cuts control latency by $35$--$47\%$ versus token-wise serial decoding and $6$--$7\%$ versus an idealized chunked engine; an H800 repetition preserves the ordering.

_all_articles.title: Learned Control Variates for Rare Grid-Outage Estimation at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
_all_articles.title_original: Learned Control Variates for Rare Grid-Outage Estimation at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public charging of electric vehicles (EVs) adds a large and synchronized load to the distribution feeders. In most networks, it is rare to overload a feeder at the same time. When it does happen, the consequences can be severe: an overloaded feeder stresses its transformers and can trigger cascading outages across a city. Planners who design for high reliability therefore need to estimate very small outage probabilities. To that end, plain Monte Carlo estimation with an expensive grid simulator can require a prohibitively large number of runs for this task. To reduce the number of runs, we propose a control variate (CV) built from a learned classifier of the outage, trained on cheap observable features such as temperature and load forecasts. We show that for any binary learner, the variance reduction is an explicit function of its recall and false-positive rate. Furthermore, we show that control variate based on a Gaussian proxy of the load loses its effect as outages become rarer, while a learner with non-vanishing precision keeps removing a fixed fraction of the variance even in the extreme rare-event regime. We verify these results in numerical experiments using a feeder-overload simulator across three orders of magnitude of outage probability and obtain that even weak learner with a single feature can remove a quarter of the variance, while a boosted-tree learner is able to remove about 60%. We then apply the estimator to the feeder network of Surabaya, Indonesia, in which the Gaussian load model leaves every feeder three to seven times the one-day-in-ten-years blackout target. At the same simulation budget, planning the reserve with the learned CV and a 95% confidence limit reduces the city-wide blackout days by a third compared with Monte Carlo. These results show that learned control variates can help planners design distribution grids that stay reliable against rare outages.

_all_articles.title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
_all_articles.title_original: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aggressive low-state weight quantization can substantially reduce neural-network representational flexibility, making predictive performance difficult to preserve when only a few discrete weight states are available. We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization. Two tasks predict either the next hour or the next 24 hours from the preceding 48 hours across two co-primary electricity-consumption datasets. Direct post-training quantization (PTQ) increased mean normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) relative to full precision by 6.25 and 7.04 percentage points in Datasets A and B, whereas quantization-aware fine-tuning (QAT-FT) recovered approximately 90.2% and 94.5% of these penalties. Quantization-aware training from random initialization (Scratch-QAT) also produced competitive low-state solutions, with particularly favorable behavior at three states. We further introduce accumulated-update thresholding, which accumulates optimizer-proposed weight changes before commitment. Relative to paired Scratch-QAT controls, this reduced committed shadow-weight updates by approximately 99.7% and discrete state transitions by approximately 77--80%, while mean NRMSE changed by only +0.042 and +0.197 percentage points. These results show that useful Transformer forecasting can be retained under highly discrete weight representations while strongly suppressing target-state activity, supporting a prospective route toward compact, low-activity edge forecasting using multilevel synaptic devices.

_all_articles.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
_all_articles.title_original: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. We propose LightCRS, a lightweight, query-conditioned framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses this evidence for each dialogue via query-conditioned cross-attention, whose parameters are shared across all domains, and compares candidates jointly with an inter-candidate Transformer. To enable rigorous evaluation, we construct MM-R2A-25, a 25-domain benchmark pairing natural Reddit recommendation-seeking conversations with Amazon product listings. LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR, improving HR@1 by 35.4\% over the strongest baseline while reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2\% over separately trained single-domain models.

_all_articles.title: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space
_all_articles.title_original: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Object: Motion artefacts remain a major limitation of routine two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) brain MRI, reducing diagnostic confidence and often necessitating repeated acquisitions. MoSAIK (Motion Search with AI in K-space) retrospectively estimates in-plane rigid-body motion directly from standard multi-coil TSE k-space. Without a motion-free reference, external navigators, or additional acquisitions, MoSAIK infers motion from k-space self-consistency violations and incorporates predicted parameters into model-based, motion-aware reconstruction rather than synthesizing corrected images. Materials and Methods: Selected complex coil data were represented as log-magnitude and phase channels. A decoupled convolutional embedding and Transformer encoder estimated phase-encoding-line-indexed rotation and two-dimensional translations. Training used motion-free clinical acquisitions with simulated motion; four held-out subjects were evaluated. Component-wise errors assessed estimation; SSIM and PSNR in silico and entropy focus criterion (EFC) in vivo assessed reconstruction. Results: Motion estimation errors were low for both rotation (MSE $<$ 0.2 deg$^2$) and translation (MSE $<$ 0.2 pixels$^2$), with Pearson correlations of approximately 0.96 and 0.94, respectively. In every in-vivo acquisition, more than 75% of slices showed information gain relative to uncorrected reconstructions. MoSAIK reduced visible artefacts while preserving anatomical detail. Discussion: Transformer-based k-space motion-trajectory estimation enables fast retrospective correction of standard clinical TSE brain MRI.

_all_articles.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
_all_articles.title_original: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at $4\times10^9$ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. We present an artificial neural network model that maps the unordered multi-set of molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio $I(t)/I_0$ in 1-3 milliseconds. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Each constituent is embedded with a chemistry-pretrained transformer language model, ChemBERTa. In our proposed method, training data are produced by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using the radiation source at 30, 80, 100, and 120 kV tube voltages over polyethylene-based shielding composite slabs of thicknesses spanning 0.15-2.5 mm. After preprocessing, the dataset contains $n = 4697$ simulated configurations on which a leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation is performed, attaining mean squared error MSE = $(1.12 \pm 0.56)\times10^{-4}$, normalized-MSE percentage NMSE% = 0.0294% $\pm$ 0.0147%, and $R^2 = 0.9988$. The corresponding per-sample percentage errors give an alpha-trimmed ($\alpha = 0.10$) absolute percentage error (APE) of 1.66% and a median APE of 1.15%. Our model's inference is several orders of magnitude faster than the underlying Monte Carlo simulation (sub-millisecond per query vs. several hours for the reference run) with effective accuracy in predicting $I(t)/I_0$.

_all_articles.title: ArcFlow: Training Flow Policies for Multiple Solver Budgets
_all_articles.title_original: ArcFlow: Training Flow Policies for Multiple Solver Budgets
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flow-matching policies adjust inference cost through the number of solver steps, but reinforcement learning at a single fixed solver budget can hide degradation at cheaper deployment budgets and even erase useful one-step behavior present in a pretrained policy. We introduce Action-Ratio-Clip Flow (ArcFlow), a deployment-aware algorithm for training one flow policy across a specified range of solver budgets. ArcFlow combines action-aligned supervision, budget exposure, and worst-budget checkpoint selection. For reconstruction objectives, its bridge aggregates temporal probes into one surrogate ratio and one PPO-style clip per action, with a boundary residual exactly equal to deployed one-step reconstruction error. Cycling exposes the shared field to the deployment range, and selection optimizes its performance floor. For native velocity objectives, multi-budget endpoint supervision applies the same principle without replacing the native update. Both realizations preserve the architecture and deployment-time cost. Across DM Control, manipulation, and locomotion, ArcFlow attains the highest mean one-step return among five flow-policy baselines on 25 of 30 tasks under each method's reported training settings. Component studies identify complementary improvements from boundary supervision, the fixed-grid bridge, budget exposure, and deployment selection. These results establish deployment-budget-aware training as an effective route to strong low-step control with one policy serving multiple inference costs.

_all_articles.title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
_all_articles.title_original: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
_all_articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) routinely report state-of-the-art accuracy. We ask how these results compare with inexpensive baselines run on the same splits. On the splits of three recent studies, we tune four baseline representatives with validation-only selection and compare them with the highest mean that each paper reports for an LLM-based method in the matched setting. Correct & Smooth on TF-IDF features trails this reference by a median of 2.3 percentage points, and an MLP on frozen e5-large-v2 embeddings by 2.8 points. Correct & Smooth is within 3 points of the reference or better on 15 of 24 tasks, but the reference is significantly higher on 12 of 22 testable tasks, so several reported gains remain substantial. Reading released code next to the papers, we also document evaluation risks: selection of hyperparameters or checkpoints on the test set, labels of test-pool nodes used in training, baseline numbers reused without disclosure, and a text-label misalignment in a released Cora loader. Reports of the same method on the same split also differ by up to 12.5 points across papers whose configurations are not documented to match.
